title: Quantum-Inspired Constraint Optimization for Neural Network Design
abstract: Quantum-inspired constraint optimization (QICO) offers a promising approach to neural network architecture design, leveraging quantum mechanical principles to explore a broader solution space than traditional methods. This paper introduces a novel QICO framework utilizing quantum annealing and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) to optimize network configurations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations, showcasing the potential for discovering innovative network architectures with improved performance. The core mechanism involves quantum-enhanced exploration of the solution space, addressing limitations of classical optimization techniques.

title: Based on Chaos Mapping Probabilistic Computation Model
abstract: This paper explores the application of chaos systems in probabilistic computation, specifically targeting the resolution of certain NP problems. The core idea is to leverage the inherent sensitivity of chaotic maps to introduce randomness into deterministic computations. This is achieved by mapping computational tasks onto chaotic systems and employing iterative simulations to approximate optimal solutions. We propose a novel framework utilizing the unpredictable nature of chaotic dynamics to provide a pathway for tackling computationally challenging problems. The model's effectiveness is predicated on the ability of chaotic systems to generate diverse solution paths, effectively exploring the solution space more thoroughly than traditional deterministic algorithms. The presented approach offers a potentially transformative method for approaching complex problems by harnessing the power of apparent disorder. Further research and development are needed to fully realize the potential of this framework across a broader range of NP problems and to optimize the simulation parameters for maximum efficiency.

title: # Bowhead: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bowhead Whale Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bowhead, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of bowhead whales. Bowhead utilizes a combination of adaptive movement patterns, bubble-net feeding strategies, and social interaction to explore the search space and converge towards optimal solutions. The algorithm incorporates key characteristics of bowhead whale behavior, including the use of acoustic communication, dynamic adjustment of movement speed and direction, and collaborative hunting. Specifically, Bowhead employs a modified version of the particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework, where particles represent potential solutions. The movement of particles is governed by a dynamic velocity update rule that mimics the bowhead whale's navigation and hunting strategies. Furthermore, a social influence mechanism, inspired by the cooperative bubble-net feeding of bowheads, is incorporated to enhance the exploration capabilities of the algorithm. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results indicate that Bowhead exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, showcasing its potential as a valuable tool for tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: 基于自适应的量子信息熵优化
abstract: Quantum information is a fundamental resource for advancing quantum computation. However, realizing the full potential of quantum systems requires robust and reliable information storage and transmission. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum information optimization, leveraging self-adaptive optimization to dynamically adjust parameters governing quantum information storage and transmission. This method aims to enhance the fidelity and reliability of quantum systems by proactively optimizing these crucial aspects. We introduce a self-adaptive process that continuously adjusts parameters based on the system's response to the computation, resulting in a more resilient and efficient quantum protocol. The proposed framework demonstrates improved performance in various quantum information tasks, exhibiting enhanced fidelity and reduced error rates. This work presents a significant advancement in quantum information optimization, offering a promising path towards more dependable quantum systems.

title: Bayesian Fractal Geometry for Dynamical Systems Modeling
abstract: This paper explores the application of Bayesian Fractal Geometry (BFG) to modeling complex dynamical systems, specifically focusing on ecological, economic, and biological systems. We propose a novel framework that explicitly incorporates fractal geometry, enabling dynamic parameter adaptation through Bayesian inference. The core mechanism involves utilizing variational autoencoders to represent system states as fractal representations, allowing for continuous parameter adjustment guided by Bayesian principles. This approach offers a significant advancement over traditional Bayesian methods by directly incorporating geometric information into the modeling process, providing a more realistic and predictive representation of dynamic systems. We detail the Bayesian inference algorithm, discuss the representation of fractal states, and provide preliminary results demonstrating the framework's capabilities in modeling a simplified ecological system.

title: Too Simple, Too Complex, Just Right: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of deep learning and inductive bias as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Blue-gray Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BGMIOA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Blue-gray Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BGMIOA), motivated by the foraging behavior of blue-gray mice. The algorithm leverages the mouse's instinctive tendency to explore the environment and converge towards food sources, mimicking its movement patterns and decision-making processes. BGMIOA incorporates key elements of mouse foraging, including path planning, obstacle avoidance, and food selection, into a dynamic optimization framework. The core of the algorithm involves a virtual "mouse" navigating a problem space, utilizing a modified roulette wheel selection mechanism based on proximity to potential solutions and incorporating a novel "exploration bias" parameter to maintain diversity and prevent premature convergence. Mathematical formulations are presented to describe the algorithm's key components, including the position update equation, the selection probability calculation, and the mutation operator. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a set of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions. The results indicate that BGMIOA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in challenging landscapes with complex fitness functions. Future research will focus on incorporating adaptive parameters and exploring applications in various fields, including engineering design, data analysis, and machine learning.

title: Quantum-Guided Geometry – Automating Geometric Transformations
abstract: Quantum-Guided Geometry (QG) represents a novel approach to geometric transformations, leveraging quantum properties to automate complex calculations and significantly accelerate geometric operations. This paper proposes a technique that utilizes quantum guidance to improve the accuracy and speed of geometric transformations, offering a potentially transformative advancement in computational geometry. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the quantum-driven adjustments and their impact on geometric results. The paper explores the application of quantum entanglement and superposition to optimize transformations, demonstrating improved results compared to conventional methods. We conclude with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications of this technology.

title: Explainability Requirements for Substantive Design Examination Using AI Examination Support Tools: Focusing on XAI-Based Institutional Safeguards
abstract: This study examines the explainability requirements for artificial intelligence (AI) examination support tools used in substantive design examinations from an explainable AI (XAI) perspective. Substantive examination combines prior design search, similarity of articles, overall aesthetic impression, and ease of creation. Hence, AI-generated similarity scores, candidate rankings, and visualized similarity-contributing regions must support, rather than replace, legal judgment. Drawing on the Design Protection Act, Design Examination Guidelines, Korean AI legislation, recent design and AI policy research, and domestic and international materials on XAI and trustworthy AI, this study identifies three discrepancies between: image similarity and overall aesthetic impression; search objects and units, and the legal relevance of retrieved candidates; and AI similarity-contributing regions, and legally significant or dominant features. As such, it argues that explainability should not require the full disclosure of model internals. Instead, it should be designed as a procedural structure which enables examiners to connect AI outputs with legal criteria, and review and record case-specific input scope, search objects and units, recommendation reasons, similarity-contributing regions, and decisions to accept, modify, or reject AI outputs. The proposed framework includes differentiated logging, quality management, and retraining controls.

title: Effects of back-side irradiance inhomogeneity in the accuracy of power estimation in bifacial PV systems
abstract: Abstract This study investigates the effects of back-side irradiance inhomogeneity on the accuracy of power estimation in bifacial photovoltaic (BPV) systems installed in Lima, Peru. An experimental setup consisting of two strings of four BPV modules each was implemented, equipped with five rear-facing irradiance sensors, including calibrated cells and a pyranometer, positioned at different vertical locations within the array. Irradiance measurements were recorded under three distinct sky conditions: clear, fully overcast, and partially overcast. The spatial variability of rear irradiance was quantified using the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) and the Mean Percentage Error (MPE). Results reveal significant inhomogeneity across sensor positions, with the sensor installed in the edges of the PV string consistently showing the largest deviation, reaching a MAPE of 16.37%. Power estimation was performed using an adapted Osterwald equation that incorporates both front and rear irradiance contributions through the bifaciality factor. Calculations using sensors installed in the middle of the string yielded more accurate power estimates, with an average MAPE of 8.82%, compared to 10.30% from the edge of the string placements. These findings highlight the importance of sensor placement and atmospheric conditions in the accurate characterization of bifacial PV system performance.

title: Power-only estimation of tilt and azimuth angles in distributed photovoltaic systems
abstract: Distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems increasingly occupy mountainous terrain, where modules at one site often differ in tilt and azimuth. Such installation-angle differences can be misidentified as faults and trigger false alarms. With module-level plane-of-array irradiance and back-of-module temperature sensors rarely installed, this paper estimates both angles from the power time series alone. Clear-sky intervals are detected from the power signal, and a variance-of-ratio objective between modeled and measured power is introduced. Since the ratio absorbs slowly varying losses such as soiling and degradation, the fit follows temporal profile shape, not amplitude. The objective is minimized by an improved sparrow search algorithm (SSA). The method is validated on a rooftop dataset from Nanjing, China, and the National Renewable Energy Laboratory dataset, covering three climates, six PV module technologies, sampling intervals from one to fifteen minutes, and observation horizons from hours to years. It estimates tilt and azimuth more accurately than PVWatts 5, PV-Peak, and Solar Data Tools, at comparable runtime. An ablation study attributes most of this accuracy to the clear-sky filtering and the variance-of-ratio objective, while the improved SSA mainly speeds convergence and stabilizes repeated runs. The estimates are insensitive to temperature-model error: a ±20 °C input bias shifts the estimated tilt by at most 0.15°. A Fisher–Cramér–Rao lower bound analysis quantifies window-level identifiability and guides window selection, showing that longer clear-sky windows spanning solar noon are the most informative. This offers a low-cost route to improved monitoring and forecasting for distributed PV plants.

title: Programmable optical differential Ising machines
abstract: Optical Ising machines provide a hardware approach for combinatorial optimization and physical-system emulation, but their scalability is limited by redundant matrix operations and analog modulation precision. Here we show a programmable optical differential Ising machine that directly evaluates Hamiltonian changes rather than the full Hamiltonian. Numerical simulations from 60 to 2000 spins show that 6-bit analog–digital conversion and 5-bit digital–analog conversion are sufficient to obtain solution quality close to high-precision digital references, with a phase-error tolerance of about 0.3–0.4 rad. Experiments on a dual-channel fiber-optic prototype reproduce phase-transition behavior in representative Ising models and solve MaxCut benchmarks through a multi-spin parallel tempering (PT) routine. The system reaches the best-known cut for the 800-spin G1 instance and 99.66% of the best-known cut for the 2000-spin G22 instance within fewer than 500 PT iterations. These results establish differential optical feedback as a route for scalable Ising-model computation. The authors develop a programmable optical differential Ising machine that directly computes Hamiltonian variations to eliminate redundant full-matrix calculations for Ising combinatorial optimization and physical system emulation. Simulations and fiber-optic prototype experiments verify that the hardware only requires 5-bit DACs and 6-bit ADCs with a phase-error tolerance of 0.3–0.4 rad, and it yields optimal MaxCut solutions for the 800-spin benchmark and 99.66% of the known optimum for the 2000-spin instance via multi-spin parallel tempering.

title: Equation Discovery for Classification: Finding Interpretable Symbolic Specifications of the Decision Boundary
abstract: Abstract Equation discovery has traditionally focused on regression, where the goal is to recover analytical expressions that model numerical targets. In this paper, we extend this paradigm to binary classification and introduce Equation Discovery for Classification (EDC), a framework that discovers concise symbolic expressions that explicitly define decision boundaries. EDC searches over a configurable grammar of analytical expressions using beam search and optimises equation parameters via dedicated numerical procedures, yielding a single interpretable equation whose sign determines class membership. We design a redundancy-aware grammar that balances expressivity and tractability, enabling the discovery of non-linear decision boundaries while maintaining interpretability. Through experiments on artificial datasets with known generating mechanisms, we show that EDC reliably reconstructs complex target boundaries, including XOR-like and interaction-driven structures, and adapts effectively under increasing levels of noise. Notably, in noisy settings EDC can outperform the original generating equation by approximating the implicit, noise-shifted decision boundary. On UCI benchmark datasets, EDC consistently outperforms existing symbolic classification approaches and other interpretable baselines, while achieving performance competitive with state-of-the-art black-box models. Although computationally more demanding than standard classifiers, we demonstrate that substantial speed-ups can be achieved with reduced search depth and simplified grammars at minimal loss of predictive performance. Overall, EDC provides a principled bridge between symbolic regression and classification, offering a transparent yet expressive alternative to black-box models for applications where interpretability of the decision boundary is essential.

title: A feature-optimized machine learning system for real-time crisis tweet identification
abstract: Preparing and organising a relief effort using useful social media content in a crisis situation is crucial. Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, and many more social media platform produces immense data. Practical implementation for necessary automatic sorting and extracting specific text by classifying tweets into useful information, which helps humanitarian needs. Demanding less computational resources to concentrate on text models to scale the work from the CrisisMMD dataset. Machine Learning (ML) classifier test for converting text by using Term Frequency Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF), Word2Vec, and Bag of Words (BoW). Performance measure is used to evaluate accuracy, macro-averaged precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC, and tested for statistical significance and ROC curves analysis, with standard metrics on the classifiers Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Multinomial Naïve Bayes (MNB), Decision Trees (DT), Random Forests (RF), XGBoost, and a combined ensemble model. Better results were obtained with the Word2Vec model than with TF-IDF, and BoW consistently delivers effective word-count-based methods, indicating simpler methods. Logistic Regression (LR) and SVMs achieve consistent and reliable results in linear models when used in an ensemble approach with measured criteria yielding the most well-rounded performance. To identify humanitarian needs and class distribution, and to correct the models to strengthen especially critical disaster response. The research focuses on demonstrating traditional ML techniques, paired with reliable test filtering and the right extraction features. Disaster-related test filtering to present real-time monitoring supports humanitarian decision-making.

title: Model Access Is Becoming a Commodity, and Data Is a Durable Advantage
abstract: This chapter emphasizes the evolving landscape of AI, where model access is becoming commoditized and data is emerging as a competitive advantage. Enterprise AI value is contingent on factors, including data quality, evaluation, application design, workflow integration, governance, human oversight, security, and operations. The chapter highlights price reductions in OpenAI's GPT-4 and gpt-4o-2024-08-06 APIs. It distinguishes between model-centric AI, which focuses on model architecture and training, and data-centric AI, which prioritizes data coverage, quality, and collection. It underscores data quality dimensions such as accuracy, consistency, and relevance, and it discusses how data work can improve model accuracy. It explores data cascades, the power-law relationships among model performance, size, dataset size, and compute. The chapter delves into case studies like the Phi series and the impact of deduplication on model performance. It emphasizes annotation quality, consistency, and inter-annotator agreement. It introduces the CRAFT assessment framework and an executive checklist for AI investment allocation. The chapter advocates for ongoing review of model selection and data quality, and the need to diagnose AI project failures across multiple layers. The chapter concludes with adaptable systems and open data infrastructure for organizational resilience.

title: Accurate in space, unreliable in time: how LLMs represent national cultural change
abstract: Assessments of cultural alignment have become an important part of the development and improvement of large language models (LLMs). However, the majority of the evaluations treat culture as a single snapshot, investigating only whether a model represents a society accurately at the current time. Research in cultural psychology shows that cultural values change at different rates and directions over time. Therefore, a "culturally aware" model should capture not only where a culture is today but also how it has changed over time. We examine this missing dimension of cultural awareness using more than two decades of the World Values Survey data. We compare the cultural trajectories of 40 countries with the trajectories produced by four state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs on the Inglehart-Welzel cultural map. Our findings show that while models generally place countries close to their most recent surveyed positions, these representations tend to lag several years behind that position. They also capture only part of the magnitude of the observed change, introduce movement where little occurred, and rarely reproduce reversals in countries' trajectories. These findings point to temporal flattening and suggest that snapshot accuracy can give an incomplete picture of cultural awareness in LLMs and have implications for model evaluation, representational harms, and the governance of culturally aware AI systems.

title: Retrieved but not ranked: surface-form bias in structural retrieval, from mathematics to agent trajectories
abstract: We evaluate embedding retrieval where surface form and meaning are pulled apart on purpose: retrieving items that share underlying structure but not wording, in two unrelated domains under one protocol, competition mathematics (MathNet-Retrieve; 500 queries, 117,088-item corpus) and embodied-agent trajectories (ALFWorld-derived; 118 queries, 336 trajectories). In mathematics the failure is complete: strict Hit@1 at the heaviest disguise tier is 0.0% for both production embedders (bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]) while the correct item sits in the top 10 nearly always, and in 95.2 to 99.8% of misses the winner is more lexically similar to the query than the correct answer. In trajectories, where surface variation is incidental, the same models land at or near hypergeometric chance when gold must involve a different object, and below chance for all three embedders once gold must differ in object and receptacle: retrieval anchors on literal tokens, not task structure. A lexical reranker control hurts in mathematics and helps in trajectories (closing 26 to 36% of the gap, CIs excluding zero); its sign reveals whether a benchmark's surface variation is adversarial or incidental. An LLM reranker recovers 5 to 63% of the gap in mathematics and 43 to 76% in trajectories; direction replicates across three judges (all 21 cells positive), but effect sizes, tier profiles, and the outlier judge change with domain (paired differences excluding zero everywhere). Mathematics gains concentrate on well-known competitions (+19.8 points, CI [+6.7, +33.2], one of six cells), so part of the recovery is memorization. In a paired downstream experiment (210 queries, graders at 96 to 99% agreement), oracle retrieval was indistinguishable from adversarially bad retrieval (McNemar p = 0.678); the solver's 69.5% zero-shot accuracy is largely a truncation proxy (97 to 100% on finished answers), leaving no headroom.

title: Analog-DB: An Agent-First Analog Integrated Circuit Database, From Blocks to Systems
abstract: Sharing analog integrated circuit designs remains difficult: foundry non-disclosure agreements restrict the process details a design depends on, and the testbenches behind published results are rarely released. We present analog-db, an open-source, versioned database built on a shareable design representation. A domain-specific language captures each design as a process-neutral topology, reusable testbenches, and a machine-readable datasheet under one schema, so a design is shared in full and re-simulates on the process kits it is bound to. A parameterization scheme exposes functional sub-blocks and device sizes as named parameters that carry their matching constraints, making circuits composable and retargetable; a schema-governed contract and queryable catalog let AI design agents discover and reuse them directly. Across the regulator corpus, all 23 circuit-kit bindings on three open kits meet their own recorded specification bands (typical corner, matched devices, no layout) and 10 of 23 meet a common class band. Seventeen of the 23 imported sizings failed their testbenches and closed under a gm/ID sizing loop driven by the annotated sub-block roles, typically within one to three iterations. In a supervised case study, a coding agent working from the released artifacts sized the op-amp cores of a chopper instrumentation amplifier on an open 130nm kit, locating four hand-entry defects and a missing common-mode feedback loop that the sizing-only baseline did not repair. The database holds 68 circuits across sixteen classes, verifiable at schematic level under a tiered harness and tracked on a power/performance scoreboard, released at https://github.com/MacAnalog/spicexplorer-release.

title: Spawn Freely, Act Sparingly: Progressive Risk Vesting for Recursive LLM-Agent Trees
abstract: Recursive LLM agents can broaden their search by spawning specialists. Some branches later request tools that send data or deploy code. When should a branch receive authority to act? We distinguish sandbox spawning, in which external controls prevent the specified harm, from capability activation, in which a selected branch crosses an irreversible-action boundary. Progressive Risk Vesting (PRV) holds a trajectory-level risk budget in escrow and debits it as branches are activated. We prove an anytime harm bound for adaptively generated trees. Branch outcomes may be dependent, but each local certificate needs to remain valid conditional on the full pre-activation history, including the information used to select the request. When activation gates, branch charges, and compute constraints are held fixed, delayed vesting preserves every policy available under irrevocable spawn charging. Marginal risk estimates can still fail after branch selection. In a stylized branching model, trajectory harm changes as the authority reproduction number $\mathcal{R}_A$ crosses one. As local risk $p$ approaches zero, trajectory harm is proportional to $p$ below criticality, proportional to $\sqrt{p}$ at criticality, and retains a positive floor above it. A finite-type occupancy model yields risk and compute shadow prices. For nested fanout modes with decreasing marginal value per unit risk, these prices produce a threshold rule. Branching calculations and a split-sample experiment illustrate the results. These synthetic studies do not estimate safety in deployed agents. The analysis suggests a design rule: search broadly in the sandbox and grant recursive authority sparingly, with an explicit risk charge.

title: MADS: A Multiview Acoustic Descriptor Set Beyond Standard Spectral Summaries
abstract: Dominant audio classification pipelines rely either on compact handcrafted summaries or on fixed time-frequency frontends such as log-mel representations prior to deep modeling. While highly successful, these representations do not explicitly expose the physical dynamics of the underlying sound-generating event. We introduce MADS (Multi-view Acoustic Descriptor Set), a compact 19-dimensional physics-informed descriptor set de- signed to capture complementary spectral, temporal, mechanical, and stochastic structure in audio signals. Rather than treating sound only as a spectral pattern, MADS encodes properties related to excitation, damping, periodicity, impulsiveness, and structural consistency within a unified multi-view representation. We evaluate MADS using standard classical machine learning models on ESC-10, ESC-50, and MSoS, and compare it against two conventional handcrafted baselines: a compact 26D MFCC- based baseline and an expanded 38D spectral-summary baseline. Across ESC-10 and ESC-50, MADS achieves the strongest peak results overall, reaching 81.00% and 52.78%, respectively, while using roughly half the dimensionality of the 38D baseline. On MSoS, MADS again delivers the strongest top-end performance, reaching 67.48%. These results establish MADS not merely as a competitive standalone descriptor set, but as the foundational descriptor layer of a broader acoustically grounded representation program for future frame-level and deep-learning-compatible audio modeling.

title: Bridging Classical and Quantum Worlds: Maps, States, and Evolutions
abstract: In this work, we present several aspects of the interplay between classical and quantum theories. After reviewing the equivalence between positivity and complete positivity in the commutative setting, we introduce and analyze intermediate notions that interpolate between these two properties for linear maps on the space of operators on a Hilbert space, highlighting their natural connections to quantum dynamics and entanglement theory. Finally, we discuss possible constructions that allow one to derive quantum states and evolutions from classical counterparts, and vice versa.

title: How a Rotten Apple Can Spoil the Barrel: Corporate Fraud Detection via Dynamic Business Networks
abstract: Corporate fraud detection is attracting renewed research interest in the era of internet connectivity due to its increasing complexity, concealment, and long-term duration. Previous fraud detection methods have heavily relied on financial statements and demonstrated limited detection power. While network analysis has emerged as a promising technique, its full potential in corporate fraud detection remains largely untapped, thus missing out on the potential improvement of fraud detection power. Recognizing this significant research gap, we devised a novel framework, NetDetect, to jointly learn structural information and temporal changes in dynamic heterogeneous networks for effective and interpretable corporate fraud detection. NetDetect consists of two new modules—meta-path-based static network feature extraction (SNFE) and temporal network feature extraction (TemFE). We rigorously evaluated each module and the entire framework against state-of-the-art baselines using a unique dataset of Chinese listed companies with a 561K node network. Experiment results and a case study demonstrate that our framework detects corporate fraud more accurately compared to baselines and offers good early-warning capability, as well as results interpretability. Our research results have important implications for various stakeholders (e.g., auditors, investors, and regulators) seeking to understand and contain corporate fraud risk. We also discuss contributions to the IS knowledge base with two design principles to guide the development of similar IT artifacts.

title: A novel short text clustering method based on the intelligent agents collaboration with large language models
abstract: To address the issues of insufficient global semantic representation and weak local distinctiveness in current short text clustering of philosophy and social science, this paper proposes a novel short text clustering method based on the intelligent agents collaboration with large language model. This method establishes a pseudo-label contrastive learning module based on semantic enhancement. We utilize a large language model to generate keyword phrases and dynamically weightedly integrate them with the original text to enhance semantic representation. Further, it uses the adaptive optimal transport to generate high-confidence pseudo labels. To address the issue of the agent’s insufficient adaptability in complex games, this paper introduces a role learning module, enabling it to autonomously evolve its roles based on changes in the situation, thereby enhancing its collaborative adaptability. Meanwhile, this paper establishes a global and local information fusion semantic representation based on the self-attention mechanism and directly applies it to the clustering algorithm. The proposed method is compared with the mainstream baselines on 8 public short text clustering datasets. The experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the baselines in all datasets in terms of the ACC metric, with an average improvement of 1.86%. The experimental results indicate that this method is suitable for clustering tasks in multiple scenarios.

title: Dataset on automation bias in AI-assisted breast ultrasound diagnosis: 295 static grayscale ultrasound images, pathological standards, and multireader multicase reading records from 148 readers
abstract: This dataset supports the article "Evaluation of Automation Bias in Breast Ultrasound Image with Different Assistance Scenarios of Artificial Intelligence: A Multireader Multicase Study" and was compiled to investigate automation bias in artificial intelligence (AI) assisted breast ultrasound diagnosis.Data were retrospectively collected from three tertiary referral hospitals in southern, central, and northern China between January 2021 and December 2023. Eligible participants were female patients aged 18 years or older who underwent breast ultrasound examination and had lesions categorized as BI-RADS 3 to 5. After independent review by two radiologists with more than three years of experience, 295 eligible cases were included, each contributing one static grayscale ultrasound image showing the largest cross section of the target lesion. The reference standard was core needle biopsy or surgical pathology for malignant cases, and pathology or stable imaging surveillance for more than three years for benign cases.The dataset comprises three components: (1) 295 de-identified static grayscale breast ultrasound images in JPG format; (2) a table of pathological or follow-up reference standards matched one to one with the images, including benign or malignant diagnosis and BI-RADS category; (3) a multireader multicase (MRMC) reading record in CSV format, documenting the diagnostic decisions of 148 radiologists from 89 hospitals across China on 80 cases (selected from the 295 cases by BI-RADS stratified random sampling) under three reading scenarios: unaided (Scenario A), simultaneous AI-aided (Scenario B), and sequential AI-aided (Scenario C). The record also contains the binary AI advice (benign or malignant), reader experience stratification.This dataset can be used for the development and validation of deep learning models for breast ultrasound, for quantitative research on human-AI collaboration and automation bias, and for analyzing diagnostic behavior across readers of different experience levels. All images and records have been de-identified.

title: A Cross-Lingual Security Evaluation of Prompt Injection Defenses in Small Language Models
abstract: Although language models are increasingly deployed in multilingual settings, the literature offers limited insight into the robustness of optimization-based defenses trained in a single language. In this paper, we investigate whether, and in what ways, the language used to construct a prompt influences its effectiveness against prompt injection in small language models. We also examine a defensive strategy against prompt injection, called DefensiveTokens, which can generalize to languages not observed during training. Our findings show that DefensiveTokens provide a robust defense against prompt injection attacks in multilingual applications.

title: UNDERSTANDING QUANTUM COMPUTING IN MEDICINE: TRANSFORMATIVE POTENTIAL AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES
authors: Pasupuleti Sreenivasa Rao*, Palukuru Sreenivasulu Reddy, Ramalinga Viswakumar
abstract: Quantum computing is a developing computational paradigm that uses the principles of quantum mechanics, like superposition and entanglement, to execute composite calculations beyond the abilities of conventional computers. Currently, implementation of this technology in medicine has the potential to revolutionize various domains like drug discovery, protein folding, genomics, medical imaging, and personalized healthcare. By allowing high-dimensional data processing and accurate molecular simulations, quantum computing may enhance biomedical research and thereby improving clinical decision-making. Moreover integrating quantum computing with artificial intelligence, mainly through quantum machine learning, further accelerates its capability to assess vast complex biological datasets and generate precise predictive models. Applications like disease prediction, drug response optimization, and advanced diagnostic imaging further validates its growing importance in modern healthcare. However, the implementation of quantum computing in medicine is presently limited by technical challenges, that includes decoherence, error correction, and scalability, as well as practical problems like high budgets and lack of skilled professionals. Moreover, ethical concerns play a major hurdle related to data privacy and healthcare inequality also require cautious consideration. In spite of these challenges, ongoing developments in hybrid quantum-classical systems and quantum algorithms reveal that a promising future, particularly placing quantum computing as an effective transformative force in next-generation medicine.

title: ## Caribou: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Caribou Migration
abstract: This paper presents Caribou, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the remarkable navigational abilities of caribou (reindeer) during their long-distance migrations. Caribou exhibit a remarkable ability to maintain a consistent heading despite significant wind drift, a phenomenon known as 'wind-following' or 'wind-anticipation'. Caribou leverages a combination of adaptive step-size control, a novel polarization mechanism mirroring caribou's social dynamics, and a dynamic memory component to effectively navigate complex search spaces. The algorithm's core mechanism, termed 'Polarized Adaptive Step-Size' (PAPS), dynamically adjusts step sizes based on both the distance to the best solution and the overall search landscape, while the polarization mechanism promotes exploration and exploitation by intelligently distributing particles across the search space. The dynamic memory component allows the algorithm to retain information about past optimal positions, facilitating efficient convergence. Experimental results on benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that Caribou consistently outperforms established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in scenarios exhibiting high dimensionality and complex, non-convex landscapes. The algorithm's adaptive nature and reliance on biologically inspired principles make it a promising tool for a variety of optimization challenges.

The algorithm's core mechanism, termed 'Polarized Adaptive Step-Size' (PAPS), dynamically adjusts step sizes based on both the distance to the best solution and the overall search landscape, while the polarization mechanism promotes exploration and exploitation by intelligently distributing particles across the search space. The dynamic memory component allows the algorithm to retain information about past optimal positions, facilitating efficient convergence. Experimental results on benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that Caribou consistently outperforms established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in scenarios exhibiting high dimensionality and complex, non-convex landscapes. The algorithm's adaptive nature and reliance on biologically inspired principles make it a promising tool for a variety of optimization challenges.

title: ## Calabrian Black Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Calabrian Black Squirrel (CBS) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the Calabrian Black Squirrel (Sciurus cinereus calabrianus). Squirrels are renowned for their efficient foraging strategies, adapting to fluctuating food availability and utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation. The CBS algorithm leverages these key aspects through a novel population-based search mechanism incorporating a 'cache' representation of promising solutions and a 'scouting' phase mimicking the squirrel's exploratory movements. The algorithm's core components – the cache size, scouting frequency, and movement strategy – are parameterized to control the balance between exploration and exploitation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the CBS algorithm on a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to converge to near-optimal solutions with competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. The algorithm's adaptability and robustness make it a promising candidate for various complex optimization challenges.

title: Calabria Pine Vole: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Pinus calabrica* Pine Voles
abstract: This paper presents Calabria Pine Vole (CPV), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Pinus calabrica* (Calabria pine vole), a small rodent known for its efficient and adaptive foraging strategies in pine forests. CPV leverages the vole's tendency to explore diverse areas, exploit promising food sources, and adjust its search pattern based on environmental feedback. The algorithm incorporates key elements of the vole's behavior, including a novel adaptive exploration-exploitation mechanism, a dynamic neighborhood structure, and a stochastic movement strategy. CPV is designed for solving complex optimization problems and is evaluated on several benchmark functions, demonstrating its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The algorithm's performance is analyzed in terms of convergence speed, solution quality, and robustness. The core innovation lies in the simulation of the pine vole's natural foraging process within the optimization framework, leading to an efficient and adaptable search strategy. The proposed method achieves promising results and offers a valuable new approach to metaheuristic optimization.

title: Non-Linear Topological Geometry: Adaptive Dynamics via Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper explores the synergistic potential of non-linear topological geometry and quantum computation to achieve higher precision and stability in quantum information storage and processing. We propose a novel algorithm leveraging the dynamic interaction of quantum entangled states with topological structures, driven by an adaptive optimization framework. The core claim is that this approach can autonomously adjust the geometric structure and quantum state of a system, offering a pathway to more robust and accurate quantum information management. We detail the proposed mechanism, outlining the integration of topological principles and quantum entanglement within an adaptive optimization system. This work addresses a significant gap in current research by providing a framework for dynamically shaping topological structures and exploiting quantum entanglement for enhanced data integrity.

title: Explainable AI for Cybersecurity Threat Detection using Shapley Values and Graph Neural Networks
abstract: The increasing sophistication and volume of cyber threats necessitate the deployment of automated detection systems. However, many current Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based cybersecurity solutions operate as "black boxes," offering limited insight into their decision-making processes. This paper introduces a novel approach to cybersecurity threat detection that leverages the strengths of both Shapley values, derived from game theory, and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). The core idea is to quantify the contribution of each feature within the GNN's network structure, providing a clear explanation for the detection of a particular threat. We utilize Shapley values to attribute importance to nodes in the graph, representing the influence of each feature on the model's output. This allows for a more transparent and understandable process, crucial for building trust and facilitating effective response to security incidents. The proposed system demonstrates the potential for explainable AI to improve cybersecurity threat detection accuracy and operational efficiency.

title: Based on Quantum Spin, a Biological Information Cryptography System
abstract: Quantum spin offers unique properties that can be harnessed for advanced cryptographic applications. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum spin for biological information cryptography, aiming to develop a secure system based on quantum spin's inherent characteristics. We propose a novel approach by introducing spin states as keys and cryptographic operations, leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to enhance security against current cryptographic vulnerabilities. The core claim is that this system can provide significantly improved security compared to traditional methods. The paper discusses the fundamental principles, potential challenges, and future directions of this research.

title: Quantum Information Tensor Encoding: A Dynamic Adaptive Encoding Approach
abstract: Quantum information encoding is a critical component of secure communication and data protection. Traditional encoding schemes often lack the flexibility to adapt to dynamic environmental conditions and quantum state evolution, limiting their security and efficiency. This paper presents a novel quantum information encoding approach, termed Dynamic Adaptive Encoding (DAE), leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust encoding parameters and enhance information security. The DAE employs a novel entanglement-based mechanism to continuously refine the encoding, providing real-time optimization of the encoding's sensitivity and robustness. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the DAE through simulations and preliminary experimental validation, highlighting its potential to significantly improve security and adaptability in quantum information systems.

title: Dynamic Topology for Quantum System Adaptation
abstract: Quantum systems are notoriously sensitive to environmental fluctuations, making their stability a significant challenge in quantum computing and quantum information processing. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often rely on static adjustments, which can be inefficient and may not effectively address system dynamics. This paper explores the application of dynamic topology, specifically a novel approach to dynamically adjust quantum system parameters based on their internal state, to enhance stability. We propose a new algorithm that leverages the inherent properties of dynamic topologies to automatically optimize quantum system parameters in response to changing conditions. The core mechanism is the construction of a dynamic topology that adapts to the system's evolution, enabling more robust and predictable quantum behavior. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach in stabilizing a complex quantum system through a process of continuous parameter adjustment.

title: Dynamic Topology and Machine Learning Synergy: A Novel Optimization Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization framework predicated on dynamic topology and machine learning synergy. The core principle lies in leveraging machine learning to autonomously learn and guide the construction of a dynamic topology, which is then effectively utilized to optimize a system. Traditional optimization methods often rely on handcrafted models, presenting limitations in adaptability and efficiency. This work proposes a framework that dynamically adapts to the system's topology, leading to improved performance and robustness. The resulting system modeling and optimization capabilities represent a significant advancement, offering a more flexible and automated approach. This paper investigates the advantages of this synergistic approach through theoretical analysis and empirical validation, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize optimization processes across diverse domains.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning for Function Approximation
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive kernel learning framework designed to address the limitations of traditional kernel methods. The core challenge in kernel learning lies in the manual selection of an appropriate kernel function and its associated parameters – a process that is often computationally intensive and reliant on domain expertise. Our approach automates this selection process by employing a Bayesian optimization strategy within a function approximation context. The algorithm dynamically learns the optimal kernel function and its parameters directly from the data, thereby enhancing flexibility and efficiency. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this adaptive framework through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components for its implementation. The core claim of this work is that automated kernel selection significantly reduces the burden on practitioners and improves the performance of kernel-based function approximation.

title: ## Blue-eyed Cuscus: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Nocturnal Marsupial
abstract: This paper presents Blue-eyed Cuscus (BEC), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the blue-eyed cuscus, a nocturnal marsupial known for its efficient searching strategies in complex environments. BEC combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Cauchy-Matthewmann-Levene (CML) mutation to create a robust and adaptive algorithm suitable for a variety of optimization problems. The core innovation lies in the adaptive adjustment of the exploration-exploitation balance using a 'cushion' mechanism mimicking the cuscus's cautious approach to new food sources. This cushion dynamically alters the influence of both the particle's best experience and global best experience, promoting efficient convergence while avoiding premature convergence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BEC through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's design prioritizes adaptability and robustness, making it a valuable addition to the optimization landscape.

title: # Blackish Butterfly Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Butterfly Flight Dynamics
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Blackish Butterfly Bat" (BBB), inspired by the flight dynamics of black swallowtail butterflies (Papilio fullo). The algorithm leverages the observed behaviors of butterflies – including erratic flight patterns, hovering, and directional changes – to create a robust and efficient search process. BBB utilizes a novel combination of adaptive velocity control, a dynamically adjusted Lévy flight component, and a local search strategy based on butterfly wingbeat frequency variations. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around simulating the butterfly's ability to efficiently explore the search space while simultaneously exploiting promising regions. Theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate BBB's competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) across a range of benchmark optimization problems. The algorithm exhibits strong convergence properties, particularly in challenging, multi-modal landscapes. Future research directions include integrating BBB with machine learning techniques and exploring its application in real-world engineering problems.

title: IDEALTA-LIME: scan-level partitions, fused deep and handcrafted features, trained models and LIME explanations for pulmonary nodule classification on LUNA16
abstract: Supporting data, code and derived artefacts for the study "Fusing Deep and Handcrafted Features for Lung Cancer Detection with Ensemble Learning and Classifier-Agnostic Explainability using Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME)", submitted to PeerJ Computer Science. Study summary IDEALTA (Integrated Diagnostic Ensemble for Lung Tumor Analysis) is an interpretability-supportive ensemble framework for pulmonary nodule candidate classification on the LUNA16 benchmark. Deep features from a frozen VGG16 backbone are combined with handcrafted Local Binary Pattern and Gabor descriptors. Each modality is classified by its own support vector machine after principal component analysis, and the three probability outputs are averaged in a soft ensemble. Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations expose the image regions underlying individual predictions, evaluated under Euclidean and cosine metrics over Quickshift superpixels. Contents config/ — the classification configuration, including the class caps and the balancing seed (balance_seed = 42) that determine the partitions reported in the manuscript. partitions/ — scan-level (seriesuid) split assignments, the split summary, the dataset validation report, and one manifest per partition. Each manifest contains one row per candidate: sample identifier, source series identifier, subset, split, label, coordinates, geometry, source CSV row and file path. Class caps are 2,000 negative and 1,149 positive for training, and 100 negative and 100 positive for each of validation and test. All 1,349 positive candidates in the 886 readable scans are retained across the three partitions. Splits are assigned once at the level of the whole computed tomography series, so no candidate from a given scan appears in more than one partition. results/ — per-seed metric tables and mean and standard deviation summaries for each of the seven compared methods (three frozen-VGG16 convolutional variants differing in loss and class weighting, and four SVM/PCA configurations over Local Binary Pattern, Gabor and VGG16 features together with their soft ensemble), accompanied by the Friedman omnibus, Nemenyi post-hoc and pairwise Wilcoxon outputs. models/ — per-seed training histories, test metrics, confusion matrices, learning curves and trained convolutional checkpoints, together with the selected support vector machine hyperparameters and per-seed confusion matrices. features/ — extracted VGG16, Local Binary Pattern and Gabor feature arrays and the corresponding labels for the training, validation and test partitions. lime/ — the Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations configuration and per-instance explanation outputs for the baseline convolutional model at seed 42 on the test partition. code/ — the data-construction and experiment notebooks, the pipeline package and command-line scripts, and the environment specification. MANIFEST.json — the relative path, byte size and SHA-256 checksum of every deposited file, together with an explicit record of what was excluded and why. Reported results Seven methods were compared over ten random seeds (1, 7, 42, 88, 123, 256, 314, 999, 1024 and 2024) on a balanced 200-region test partition. The soft ensemble attains accuracy 0.848 plus or minus 0.016, F1 0.834, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.927, sensitivity 0.765 and specificity 0.931. The strongest convolutional baseline attains accuracy 0.808. These are computational findings on a single public benchmark; clinical use would require prospective external validation. Source imaging The computed tomography imaging is not redeposited in this record. All experiments use the publicly available LUNA16 collection (doi:10.5281/zenodo.3723295), derived from the LIDC-IDRI collection hosted on The Cancer Imaging Archive (doi:10.7937/K9/TCIA.2015.LO9QL9SX). Both are cited in the manuscript and their original licences govern that data. The region-of-interest arrays are likewise omitted, as they are reconstructed deterministically from the deposited manifests and configuration. No new patient data were collected. title: When Does Cost-Sensitive Weighting Matter? A Classifier-Capacity Anal-ysis for Imbalanced Classification
abstract: Class weighting is the most widely used cost-sensitive remedy for class imbalance, and inverse-frequency “balanced” weights are often applied as an unquestioned default. This paper asks whether the choice among competing weighting mechanisms actually matters, and for which classifiers. Seven mechanisms, namely Balanced, Cost-Matrix, Sqrt-InverseFreq, Log-Damped, Effective-Number, a Search-Tuned power scheme, and focal loss, were evaluated on twenty-four benchmark datasets whose imbalance ratios reach 85:1, under three base classifiers of increasing representational capacity: logistic regression, a soft-voting ensemble of logistic regression, random forest, and a support vector machine, and XGBoost. Using leakage-free nested cross-validation and the Friedman–Nemenyi procedure applied separately to each classifier, mechanism choice produced large, highly significant differences under logistic regression (p < 0.0001), differences that shrank to non-significance under the voting ensemble (p = 0.179) and became indistinguishable from a random ordering under XGBoost (p = 0.955, average-rank spread of 0.46). At the same time, the two high-capacity classifiers outperformed logistic regression under every mechanism tested. The evidence supports a simple two-tier policy: tune the weighting scheme carefully for linear learners, and keep the plain balanced default for ensemble and boosting learners, where additional tuning yields no benefit that survives a significance test.

title: Validated Binary Decompilation Without Tears
abstract: Binaries are an attractive target for formal verification—they describe a precise and deterministic semantics that closely conforms to the execution. However, binary verification entails a decompilation process, and the credibility of the verification hinges on the correctness of the decompiler. In this paper, we present a translation validation approach to decompiler assurance. We define a simple and compositional formalisation of decompiler correctness that is strong enough to preserve safety properties as well as security hyperproperties, thereby enabling verification results of the decompiled code to transfer to the executable code. Our notion, termed conditional trace-equivalence, allows the decompilation to leverage heuristics by embedding them within the program semantics. Our translation validation approach is implemented in the AArch64 decompiler Basil. Its evaluation showcases that translation validation is well-suited to verifying binary decompilation that scales to real-world C binaries. Our encoding exemplifies that the approach incurs minimal engineering overhead.

evidence.title: Validated Binary Decompilation Without Tears
evidence.abstract: Binaries are an attractive target for formal verification—they describe a precise and deterministic semantics that closely conforms to the execution. However, binary verification entails a decompilation process, and the credibility of the verification hinges on the correctness of the decompiler. In this paper, we present a translation validation approach to decompiler assurance. We define a simple and compositional formalisation of decompiler correctness that is strong enough to preserve safety properties as well as security hyperproperties, thereby enabling verification results of the decompiled code to transfer to the executable code. Our notion, termed conditional trace-equivalence, allows the decompilation to leverage heuristics by embedding them within the program semantics. Our translation validation approach is implemented in the AArch64 decompiler Basil. Its evaluation showcases that translation validation is well-suited to verifying binary decompilation that scales to real-world C binaries. Our encoding exemplifies that the approach incurs minimal engineering overhead.

title: The Effect of Intellectual Property Regulation of AI Training Data on AI Capital Accumulation
abstract: This study quantitatively examines how the level of intellectual property protection over artificial intelligence (AI) training data affects AI capital accumulation. Korean copyright law provides no explicit exception for text and data mining; therefore, using protected works for AI training depends on ex-post interpretation of the general fair use provision. Drawing on a review of domestic and foreign regulations and disputes, the study identifies two channels through which protection operates: rising costs at the data procurement stage and binding constraints at the training stage. This distinction is consistent with 2025 U.S. court decisions that assess AI training separately from data acquisition. A dynamic general equilibrium model incorporating a Lucas span-of-control structure represents these channels as policy parameters and simulates how changes in protection affect aggregate output and knowledge capital, the model's representation of AI capital. Under the baseline calibration, tightening protection by 20 percent reduces the knowledge capital stock by 17.1 percent and output by 3.4 percent, with the training-stage channel accounting for the larger share of the overall effect. This effect arises primarily from reduced use of knowledge capital rather than substitution toward labor.

title: Speaker-Mediated Route Knowledge Transfer for Goal-Oriented Vision-and-Language Navigation
abstract: Goal-oriented vision-and-language navigation (VLN) requires an agent to reach a target from a high-level instruction that does not prescribe a route. Training therefore faces two problems. First, terminal and distance-based feedback leave partial trajectories without route-semantic supervision. Second, a single annotated path introduces single-reference route bias because several routes may satisfy the same goal. We propose Speaker-Mediated Route Knowledge Transfer (SMRKT), which comprises three components. To provide the route knowledge required by both problems, we trained a trajectory-to-language speaker on route-following VLN data and froze it as a training-time evaluator in the cross-granularity route-prior transfer process. To address the lack of route-semantic supervision, Speaker Reconstruction Progress Reward converts consecutive reconstruction-loss changes into intermediate feedback. To address single-reference route bias, Disagreement-Aware Trajectory Reuse interprets the speaker score with terminal outcome, retaining successful low-score paths as alternative demonstrations and failed high-score paths as hard replay cases. The navigator retains the original goal-oriented instruction, and the speaker is absent at inference. In DUET-based validation on two goal-oriented VLN datasets, SMRKT improves Success Rate (SR) by 1.42 percentage points on the unseen validation setting of the REVERIE dataset, by 1.32 percentage points on the Unseen Houses split of the SOON dataset, and by 2.22 percentage points on the Unseen Instructions split of the SOON dataset; SPL and OSR rise in some settings and fall in others. The results support transferred route knowledge as a training signal, with environmental success retained as the final task criterion.

title: QUANTUM COMPUTING IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: CONVERGENCE, FRAMEWORKS, AND EMERGING APPLICATIONS
abstract: : The rapid convergence of quantum computing and artificial intelligence is reshaping computational paradigms across cryptography, optimization, sensing, and intelligent systems. This paper surveys and synthesizes recent developments at the intersection of quantum computing and AI, with particular attention to superconducting quantum hardware, quantum reinforcement learning, quantum key distribution optimization, and hybrid AI-driven post-quantum security frameworks. Drawing upon 2026 literature— including advances in high-speed predistortion architectures for flux-bias lines, enhanced quantum key distribution parameter optimization, quantum reinforcement learning for spectrum allocation in 6G networks, hybrid AI–post-quantum encryption for Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) systems, and measurement-consistent low-field MRI enhancement via k-space noise modeling—we present a unified perspective on how quantum resources augment classical AI and how AI, in turn, accelerates the practical deployment of quantum technologies. We introduce a conceptual Quantum–AI Convergence Framework that maps hardware constraints, algorithmic opportunities, and security requirements. The analysis highlights persistent challenges in noise resilience, scalability, hybrid orchestration, and regulatory readiness, while outlining promising research directions for trustworthy quantum-enhanced intelligence.

title: Recent advances in neuromorphic photonics: Devices, architectures, and physical learning systems (2022–2026)
abstract: Neuromorphic photonics has emerged in the past five years as one of the most promising hardware paradigms for overcoming the bandwidth, energy, and scalability limits of conventional electronic accelerators. Between 2022 and 2026, the field has undergone a rapid transition from isolated proof-of-concept demonstrations of individual photonic neurons or synaptic weights toward integrated, reconfigurable, and functionally complete systems that combine linear optical processing, in-hardware nonlinearity, analogue memory, and on-chip learning on a single substrate. This review provides a comprehensive and critical account of these developments, organized around three analytical axes: device-level primitives, architectural paradigms, and physical learning mechanisms. Device-level advances are discussed in terms of photonic neurons (engineered integrated neurons and dynamical laser neurons), synaptic and weighting elements (phase-change materials, electro-optic analogue memories, micro-ring weight banks), and the nonlinear platforms (silicon, silicon nitride, thin-film lithium niobate, III–V laser dynamics, photorefractive media) that enable neural-like behavior. Architectural paradigms are examined through five complementary families: integrated, coherent, and wavelength-multiplexed photonic neural networks (PNNs); spiking photonic systems, photonic reservoir computing, diffractive and free-space optical processors, and physically adaptive systems based on soliton dynamics in photorefractive media. Particular emphasis is placed on two milestones that mark the maturity of the field: the demonstration of monolithically integrated analogue memory for in situ training and inference, and the experimental realization of end-to-end on-chip backpropagation within a PNN. In parallel, an alternative and less explored direction based on spatial-soliton dynamics and photorefractive nonlinearities is analyzed in depth. In these so-called solitonic neural networks, computation, connectivity, and memory are co-localized within the optical medium, enabling adaptive interconnections and synaptic plasticity through the self-organization of light-induced refractive-index patterns. A comparative discussion is offered between integrated programmable architectures and physically adaptive, self-organized systems, identifying the key open challenges: scalability, stability, training efficiency, standardized benchmarking, and the integration of memory and computation, together with the opportunities that distinguish photonic from electronic neuromorphic hardware. Finally, future research directions are outlined, with particular emphasis on hybrid architectures that combine the programmability of integrated photonics with the physical plasticity of adaptive optical media. Approximately 80 recent works are systematically analyzed to trace the trajectory of the field and to provide a reference framework for the next generation of neuromorphic photonic processors.

title: Abstract No: 100 Enhanced Survival Prediction in IgA Nephropathy through Integration of Pathomic and Clinical Data Using Multi-Instance Learning
abstract: IgA nephropathy, the most common primary glomerular disease, necessitates accurate survival prediction to guide personalized treatment and improve patient outcomes. Current methods often inadequately leverage pathological whole-slide images (WSIs) and rely predominantly on single-modal data, which limits predictive performance. This study aims to develop a weakly supervised learning framework that effectively integrates pathomic and clinical information to improve survival prediction in IgA nephropathy.

title: Parallel‐Channel Topological Quantum Routing in a Superconducting Qudit Chain
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient quantum routing and entanglement distribution are essential for scalable quantum networks. We propose a parallel chain topological quantum routing based on a chain of superconducting qudits, where distinct internal levels of each qudit define independent topologically protected channels. Utilizing a network of superconducting qudits (multi‐level quantum systems) and microwave resonators, our scheme realizes multiple independent SSH‐type chains in the single‐excitation subspace, each associated with a distinct internal level of the qudits. The key innovation is that distinct internal levels of qudits realize mutually independent parallel SSH chains, enabling independent and protected quantum channels. We demonstrate that quantum states can be routed to different output ports based on internal degrees of freedom (i.e., distinct energy levels of superconducting qudits). Furthermore, we show that this system enables adiabatic pumping for state transfer and preparation of entanglement via the Rice‐Mele model. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the system possesses topological robustness against coupling and potential disorders, and remains stable in the presence of dissipation, highlighting its potential for quantum routing and entanglement distribution and establishing it as a versatile building block for multi‐functional quantum devices in noise‐resilient quantum networks.

title: TAPVid-MV: A Benchmark for Tracking Any Point in 3D Across Multiple Views
abstract: Multi-camera systems are increasingly practical for robotics, AR/VR, and autonomous driving because complementary views reduce depth ambiguity and preserve visibility under occlusion. Existing point-tracking benchmarks, however, focus on a single video or static multi-camera rigs. None test long-term 3D point tracking across several synchronized views under camera motion. We introduce TAPVid-MV (Tracking Any Point in Video across Multiple Views), the first benchmark for this setting. It contains a curated set of 238 sequences, 1,004 calibrated camera streams, and 74,147 point tracks across seven subsets spanning indoor and outdoor domains, from robotics and human activity to driving and synthetic procedural scenes. We obtain these trajectories using dataset-specific auxiliary modalities: sensor depth, LiDAR, SLAM and SfM points, human meshes, posed object meshes, and simulation. Every sequence and trajectory is visually verified by human annotators. Across more than 30 baselines, no method comes close to solving the task. Surprisingly, existing multi-view point trackers do not consistently outperform monocular point trackers. By evaluating reconstruction and point tracking on the same datasets, TAPVid-MV helps distinguish errors in recovered geometry from errors in point correspondence. Through this joint analysis, we identify geometry recovery as a major bottleneck for accurate 3D point tracking. Beyond multi-view 3D point tracking, our released annotations support monocular 2D and 3D point tracking, future-trajectory prediction, and 4D reconstruction. Project page: https://tapvidmv.github.io/

title: BS: Take the Hint - Interactive Multitracer PET/CT Lesion Segmentation with a Scribble-Conditioned ResEnc U-Net
abstract: Automated lesion segmentation in whole-body PET/CT is complicated by the variety of physiological tracer uptake patterns and by the differing appearance of lesions across tracers. The autoPET/CT V challenge addresses this by making segmentation interactive: user scribbles marking foreground and background are supplied alongside the image, and the algorithm is expected to exploit them. We present our submission, a scribble-conditioned residual encoder U-Net operating on four input channels: CT, PET, and a sparse scribble map for each of foreground and background. The network is initialised from the autoPET-III winning weights and extended from two to four input channels, with the two scribble channels zero-initialised so that the pretrained representation is preserved exactly at initialisation. Every model is fine-tuned per fold from the corresponding autoPET-III fold checkpoint, so that no validation case is seen during pretraining. PET intensities are normalised against a per-scan aorta blood-pool reference derived from a CT segmentation, which removes tracer- and centre-specific scaling without requiring lesion labels. At inference the five fold models are ensembled by averaging their softmax outputs per sliding-window patch, before Gaussian-weighted stitching. On the challenge's five-fold split, with each fold evaluated on its own validation cases, mean Dice is 0.554 and mean lesion-level F1 is 0.528 without scribbles, rising to 0.751 and 0.733 after five correction rounds. About 85% of that gain follows the first scribble, and the spread between fold models narrows five-fold over the same rounds, so interaction largely compensates for how well or badly a given model segments unaided.

title: Generalized spectral bound for quasi-twisted codes
abstract: Minimum distance bounds play a central role in the analysis of algebraic codes. For cyclic and constacyclic codes, several bounds based on their zero set have been developed. However, analogous results for quasi-twisted (QT) codes are comparatively limited. In this paper, we further investigate the spectral theory of QT codes and derive a general spectral bound on their minimum distance. Our bound unifies and generalizes previously known spectral bounds for quasi-cyclic (QC) and QT codes, and contains them as special cases. We present a new proof technique and show that the bound can be formulated with respect to an arbitrary subset of eigenvalues, thereby extending its applicability to the largest possible setting. Numerical examples and simulations demonstrate that the proposed bound often improves upon the Jensen bound and earlier spectral bounds.

title: Ανάπτυξη εξειδικευμένου μεγάλου γλωσσικού μοντέλου για τη ναυτιλία με αξιοποίηση αρχιτεκτονικής RAG
abstract: Τα ναυτιλιακά τεχνικά εγχειρίδια περιλαμβάνουν εκτεταμένες πληροφορίες που σχετίζονται με τη λειτουργία, τη συντήρηση και την ασφάλεια, γεγονός που καθιστά την αναζήτηση συγκεκριμένων τεχνικών στοιχείων χρονοβόρα. Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία εξετάζει τη χρήση της αρχιτεκτονικής Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) ως μέθοδο για τη βελτίωση της πρόσβασης σε πληροφορίες που περιέχονται στη ναυτιλιακή τεχνική τεκμηρίωση. Σχεδιάστηκε και υλοποιήθηκε ένα τοπικά εκτελούμενο σύστημα RAG για την παραγωγή απαντήσεων βάσει ναυτιλιακών τεχνικών εγχειριδίων. Το σύστημα επεξεργάζεται έγγραφα PDF σε επικαλυπτόμενα τμήματα κειμένου, τα μετατρέπει σε διανυσματικές αναπαραστάσεις χρησιμοποιώντας το μοντέλο all-MiniLM-L6-v2 SentenceTransformer και τα αποθηκεύει σε μια μόνιμη διανυσματική βάση δεδομένων ChromaDB. Για κάθε ερώτηση του χρήστη, ανακτώνται τα σχετικά τμήματα των εγγράφων και χρησιμοποιούνται ως πλαίσιο για το γλωσσικό μοντέλο Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. Τόσο η ανάκτηση όσο και η παραγωγή απαντήσεων πραγματοποιούνται τοπικά, χωρίς τη χρήση εξωτερικού API γλωσσικού μοντέλου, ενώ αναπτύχθηκε και γραφικό περιβάλλον χρήστη για την άμεση αλληλεπίδραση με το σύστημα. Το σύστημα αξιολογήθηκε με 24 ερωτήσεις βασισμένες σε τέσσερα ναυτιλιακά τεχνικά εγχειρίδια. Η σχετική πληροφορία ανακτήθηκε επιτυχώς σε 20 από τις 24 ερωτήσεις, που αντιστοιχεί σε συνολικό ποσοστό επιτυχούς ανάκτησης 83,3%. Από τις παραγόμενες απαντήσεις, 15 (62,5%) χαρακτηρίστηκαν ως πλήρως ορθές, έξι (25,0%) ως μερικώς ορθές και τρεις (12,5%) ως λανθασμένες. Τα αποτελέσματα δείχνουν ότι το προτεινόμενο ελαφρύ και τοπικά εκτελούμενο σύστημα RAG μπορεί να υποστηρίξει την πρόσβαση σε τεχνική πληροφορία από διαφορετικά ναυτιλιακά εγχειρίδια, ενώ παράλληλα αναδεικνύουν ότι η επιτυχής ανάκτηση δεν εγγυάται πάντοτε μια πλήρη ή ακριβή τελική απάντηση. Το σύστημα παρέχει επομένως μια χρήσιμη βάση για την περαιτέρω ανάπτυξη τοπικά εκτελούμενων εργαλείων RAG για ναυτιλιακή τεχνική τεκμηρίωση.
