title: What, Where, and How: Probing Spatiotemporal Representations in Video Foundation Models
abstract: Self-supervised video foundation models learn rich spatiotemporal representations, yet it remains unclear what visual concepts these representations encode, where they emerge across transformer layers, and how they are geometrically organized. In this work, we tackle these three questions through a systematic layer-wise analysis of V-JEPA 2 and VideoMAE-v2. We leverage lightweight probes trained to discover three temporally grounded properties: (i) camera motion understanding, (ii) intuitive physics, and (iii) anomaly detection. Both models encode camera motion, with best results ($>90$ ROC AUC) emerging at 60-70% of network depth, and achieve moderate anomaly detection performance ($>60$ ROC AUC), but remain near chance on intuitive-physics tasks, suggesting a limited encoding of deeper physical reasoning. Beyond classification, we find that temporal features from individual videos form smooth low-dimensional trajectories in representation space, suggesting that camera motion is not only linearly decodable but also geometrically organized. Based on these results, we apply geometry-aware spline-based steering in the model's latent representations to interpolate camera motion, yielding steered videos with smoother trajectories and more coherent temporal progression than linear interpolation.

title: A Scalable Multi-Protocol Platform for Quantum Key Distribution Simulation with Rigorous Statistical Evaluation
abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) offers information- theoretically secure key establishment grounded in the laws of quantum physics, yet its practical reach is limited by the prohibitive cost of photonic hardware and the fragmented nature of existing simulation tools. Most simulators support only a single protocol and report results from individual stochastic runs, making systematic protocol comparison and reproducible statistical inference difficult. This paper presents a unified QKD simulation platform that implements four foundational protocols BB84, B92, E91, and BBM92 within a single Python/Qiskit engine. A shared impairment model covers fiber attenuation, source and detector losses, po- larization drift, and configurable intercept-resend eavesdropping. The platform is accessible through two independent interfaces that share the same backend: a desktop application (Tkinter, Matplotlib) for local experimentation and a browser-based web client (React, Node.js/Express) for zero-install remote access. All reported results are drawn from repeated-run studies (20 independent runs, 10000 qubits each), with mean, standard deviation, and 95% confidence intervals stated throughout. At a 25 km fiber link, BB84 achieves the highest mean key-rate of 160,045 Hz, followed by BBM92 (80023 Hz), E91 (52815 Hz), and B92 (40011 Hz) ordering that tracks simulation-derived sifting efficiencies precisely. Under the E91 protocol, the CHSH S-statistic averages 2.12 at baseline and falls to 1.58 when an eavesdropper is activated, demonstrating Bell-inequality-based intrusion detection independent of QBER

title: Web Price Extraction: State of the Art and an Adaptive Browserless Implementation
abstract: Price extraction from websites is a key task for market monitoring, price comparison, and business analytics in e-commerce. Existing approaches can be broadly divided into four groups, and understanding their trade-offs in accuracy and scalability is essential for selecting suitable extraction strategies. Classical methods rely on manually written wrappers and rule induction from labeled pages, offering high accuracy but adapting poorly to structural changes and requiring considerable maintenance effort. Browser-based methods, using tools such as Selenium and Puppeteer, handle dynamic JavaScript content but consume large computational resources and scale poorly. Browserless approaches retrieve HTML directly via HTTP requests, offering significant gains in speed and cost, but rely on rules calibrated for specific sites. Methods based on machine learning and large language models offer adaptability but require training data and substantial computation. Our main contribution is an adaptive browserless price extraction system that improves robustness to structural differences between websites. We implemented a baseline architecture combining HTML page fragmentation with syntactic, semantic, and frequency rules, and extended it in two ways: a Bayesian approach that dynamically updates rule weights, and a genetic algorithm that optimizes the system's global parameters. This hybrid scheme increased precision from 77.2% to 87.3% and reduced average per-page processing time by approximately 14% relative to the baseline, confirming it as a competitive alternative to manually tuned browserless solutions and to more resource-intensive browser- or LLM-based methods, offering high extraction accuracy at low computational cost.

title: Forbid Your Attention: Fooling Multimodal Large Language Models by Selectively Removing Intrinsic Focus in Spectral Domain
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have extended the capability of large language models (LLMs) to process more contextual multimodal information, showing remarkable progress in diverse realistic multimodal applications. Despite their strong perception and reasoning abilities, recent studies reveal that MLLMs remain highly vulnerable to adversarial inputs, especially those targeting visual components. However, existing attacks mainly focus on global perturbations, lacking an understanding of how MLLMs internally interpret visual structures. In this paper, we make the attempt to investigate the intrinsic focus of MLLMs in the frequency domain and discover that their predictions are particularly sensitive to phase information, which encodes essential structural and semantic cues. Based on this observation, we propose a novel phase-aware adversarial attack framework that explicitly restricts adversarial perturbations to structure-relevant phase regions to suppress the MLLMs' focus for effective and imperceptible attacks. To further amplify the structural influence, we also introduce an auxiliary adversarial prompt learning module to guide multimodal misalignment around phase-sensitive regions, misleading the MLLM's attention toward targeted structural patterns. Extensive experiments on multiple representative MLLM models and datasets demonstrate the superior effectiveness of our method compared to existing attacks.

title: A Mathematical Framework for Legacy, Governance, and Decision Integrity in Enterprise AI
abstract: Enterprise artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in decisions that must remain lawful, explainable, adaptable, and accountable despite personnel turnover, model replacement, regulatory change, and shifting organizational incentives. Existing governance frameworks provide important principles but do not by themselves supply a compact mathematical language for evaluating whether an institution can preserve sound judgment over time. This paper develops a design-science framework for institutional legacy: the durable capacity of a decision system to continue producing beneficial, lawful, explainable, and adaptable outcomes after its original designers have stepped away. The framework contributes: (i) a normalized Legacy Score based on a penalized geometric mean of knowledge retention, governance, human oversight, adaptability, feedback learning, and jurisdictional fidelity; (ii) Decision Confidence and Decision Risk models separating evidentiary confidence from consequence; (iii) authority-aware retrieval and calibrated abstention; (iv) Decision Memory for governed organizational learning; (v) Regulatory Change Velocity mapping change exposure to review intervals; and (vi) a federated regulatory knowledge-graph architecture preserving provenance and legal hierarchy. The paper also proposes eight AI Decision Integrity Rules, an evaluation protocol, and a reproducible computational demonstration. The demonstration combines a deterministic stress test with 200 Monte Carlo replications of 10,000 synthetic decisions each, illustrating Legacy Score non-compensation and comparing consequence- and authority-aware routing with a matched-coverage confidence-only baseline. The contribution remains conceptual rather than field-validated; the simulation tests internal behavior, not production performance, and all parameters require context-specific calibration.

title: Knowledge Graphs voor Machine Learning
abstract: This PhD addresses the growing fragmentation of machine learning (ML) artifacts, such as datasets, pipelines, models, and publications, which are currently siloed across diverse repository platforms. To mitigate the resulting reproducibility crisis and improve artifact discovery, the thesis proposes a unified semantic framework that leverages Semantic Web technologies to model the ML lifecycle. The core contribution is the Machine Learning Sea Knowledge Graph (MLSea-KG), a large-scale knowledge graph (KG) that integrates heterogeneous ML metadata. The thesis demonstrates how latent semantic representations of this KG can improve automated machine learning (AutoML) through a framework called KGmetaSP, which uses KG embeddings to warm-start pipeline configuration and estimate dataset similarity. Furthermore, to tackle missing or ambiguous metadata, the thesis introduces TorchicTab and RODEO, employing large language models (LLMs) and graph neural networks (GNNs) for state-of-the-art semantic table annotation. Finally, the work proposes automated declarative mapping solutions (AutoRML and Yatter) and in-memory data integration extensions to significantly reduce the manual effort required for knowledge graph construction (KGC).

title: An AI-Driven Secure Interpreter for Adaptive and Security- Aware Program Execution
abstract: Traditional programming interpreters are primarily designed to perform lexical analysis, syntax analysis, semantic processing, and program execution according to predefined programming-language rules. Although such interpreters provide reliable and deterministic execution, they generally have limited capabilities for contextual code understanding, adaptive optimization, intelligent assistance, and continuous security analysis. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), large language models (LLMs), machine learning (ML), and cloud computing provide an opportunity to transform conventional interpreters into intelligent execution environments. However, integrating AI directly into an interpreter introduces additional concerns related to malicious code execution, vulnerable AI-generated code, prompt injection, data exposure, model manipulation, privacy, and computational overhead. This paper proposes an AI-Powered Secure Intelligent Interpreter (AISII) that integrates conventional interpretation mechanisms with AI-based code understanding, vulnerability analysis, runtime behavioral monitoring, anomaly detection, secure sandboxing, adaptive policy enforcement, and cloud-assisted intelligence. The proposed architecture follows a modular, defense-in-depth approach in which source code is analyzed through lexical, syntactic, semantic, static-security, and AI-based assessment stages before execution. A runtime monitoring layer continuously evaluates execution behavior and dynamically updates a risk score. Depending on the estimated risk, the security policy engine can permit, restrict, isolate, or terminate execution. The framework further incorporates local, edge, and cloud intelligence to balance privacy, latency, and computational scalability. A comparative analysis positions the proposed architecture against conventional interpreters, AI-assisted programming tools, static analysis systems, and autonomous software-engineering agents. An experimental methodology is also proposed using code-generation benchmarks, vulnerability datasets, benign/malicious execution workloads, and real-world software-engineering tasks. Evaluation metrics include execution latency, resource utilization, vulnerability-detection precision, recall, F1-score, false-positive rate, and containment effectiveness. The paper concludes with an implementation roadmap and discusses federated learning, edge AI, autonomous programming, and quantum computing as future research directions. The proposed framework provides a foundation for developing interpreters that are not merely execution engines but adaptive, intelligent, and security-aware computing environments.

title: Avaliação de Desempenho de Algoritmos de Cifra de Fluxo para Sistemas Embarcados
abstract: Sistemas embarcados conectados a redes industriais demandam mecanismos de criptografia compatíveis com seus recursos limitados. Este trabalho compara experimentalmente as implementações de referência de quatro cifras de fluxo leves padronizadas, ChaCha20, Trivium, Rabbit e Enocoro-128v2, em uma Raspberry Pi 4, medindo tempo de cifragem, vazão, ciclos por byte e footprint de memória. O Trivium atingiu 598 MiB/s, enquanto ChaCha20, Rabbit e Enocoro-128v2 obtiveram 173 MiB/s, 232 MiB/s e 57 MiB/s. As diferenças são explicadas pelo número de operações por byte de keystream e pelo paralelismo em nível de instrução que cada função de rodada expõe ao pipeline do Cortex-A72.

title: The Egress Boundary as a Release Gate: Enforcing No-Egress in Offline Enterprise AI
abstract: Abstract. Offline enterprise AI is commonly sold on the promise that data stays local. In practice that promise is usually a policy: a statement of intent, backed by contracts and configuration, that the buyer is asked to trust. This paper argues that for sovereign deployments the property should be treated instead as an engineering invariant, something a component must demonstrate rather than something an operator must trust. We describe three complementary controls. First, a loopback-only inference engine that binds solely to the local host, ships without telemetry, and performs no background update or licence calls, so that in ordinary operation it originates no network traffic at all. Second, an operator-controlled egress gateway that is disabled by default, permits outbound connections only to an explicit allowlist, and records each decision to allow or deny as a sealed entry. Third, and centrally, a release gate that tests a component for network reachability before it is allowed to ship: a build that can reach the network does not pass. We contrast this design with policy-based and endpoint-detection approaches, which observe and react to egress rather than preventing its possibility, and we set out the limits honestly, including covert channels, side channels and the trust that must still be placed in the host kernel and hardware. No-egress, on this account, becomes a testable release criterion rather than an assurance.

title: Celaque Broad-clawed Shrew: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of a Unique Mammal
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Celaque Broad-clawed Shrew (CBS), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Notoryctes celaque*, a unique shrew species endemic to New Guinea. The algorithm leverages the observed strategies of this animal – specifically its complex and adaptive foraging patterns – to develop a robust optimization technique. CBS incorporates elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO), simulated annealing (SA), and a novel adaptive exploration-exploitation mechanism. The core of the algorithm rests on a 'territory mapping' concept, mirroring the shrew's tendency to establish and defend foraging territories. We detail the algorithm's design, including its parameters, objective function representation, and the adaptive mechanisms for adjusting exploration and exploitation. The performance of CBS is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capabilities against established metaheuristic algorithms. The results highlight the potential of bio-inspired algorithms, particularly those drawing inspiration from unusual animal behaviors, to produce novel and efficient optimization solutions.

title: Dynamic Quantum Topology Learning Algorithm: Tuning Parameters for Enhanced System Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a dynamic quantum topology learning algorithm designed to optimize system modeling through adaptive parameter adjustments. Traditional learning algorithms often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to capture complex system dynamics. Our approach dynamically adjusts quantum circuit parameters based on input data and system state, fostering a more robust and adaptable system representation. We propose a novel mechanism leveraging quantum circuit simulation to establish a direct connection between system model and topology, enabling fine-tuning and improved performance. The algorithm's core is a continuous parameter adjustment process guided by system observations.

title: Cameroon Climbing Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Cameroon Climbing Mouse Algorithm" (CCMA), inspired by the observed climbing behavior of the Cameroon climbing mouse (Peromyscus malamboensis). This rodent species exhibits remarkable agility and adaptability when traversing complex, uneven terrain. The algorithm leverages these natural climbing strategies to generate a new optimization approach. The core principle of CCMA revolves around simulating the mouse's movement by adapting a combination of particle movement strategies, including a "leap-and-explore" mechanism based on terrain slope analysis and a "cling-and-adjust" technique simulating grip maintenance. The algorithm employs a population-based search, similar to Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), but incorporates a dynamically adjusted inertia weight and velocity update rule influenced by the simulated terrain gradient. Mathematical formulations describing the key components of CCMA, including the fitness function, particle movement equations, and the algorithm's parameters, are presented. The algorithm is designed to effectively navigate complex search spaces and is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a conceptual example. The potential benefits of CCMA, particularly in tackling problems with non-convex landscapes and requiring adaptability, are discussed. Future research directions are also outlined, focusing on the algorithm's implementation and validation through comparative studies with established metaheuristic methods.

title: Burramys: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Burramy Burrowing Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Burramys, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the burrowing behavior of *Burramys* (a fictional, subterranean rodent). The algorithm mimics the exploratory and adaptive digging patterns of this creature to navigate complex search spaces. Burramys utilizes a novel combination of particle movement, local search, and a dynamic burrow network representation. The core mechanism involves simulating the creation and abandonment of burrows, with particles representing potential solutions exploring and modifying the landscape. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating competitive results compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The key innovation lies in the dynamic burrow network, which allows for efficient exploitation of promising regions while maintaining exploration capabilities. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance analysis, highlighting its strengths and potential applications.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Modulated Geometry Transformations
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize geometric modeling and simulation. We introduce a novel approach, termed "Modulated Geometry Transformations," leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve precise geometric representation and optimization. The core mechanism centers around utilizing entanglement to control and evaluate geometric transformations, offering a pathway to enhanced computational efficiency and accuracy compared to classical methods. This work presents a framework for manipulating geometric data through entangled states, facilitating the development of advanced simulations and optimization techniques. We aim to demonstrate the feasibility of this approach, highlighting its potential impact on diverse fields including computational geometry, physics simulation, and optimization.

title: Non-Linear Quantum Topology Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum system optimization based on non-linear quantum topology. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex systems exhibiting intricate geometries, leading to suboptimal solutions. This research leverages the dynamic nature of quantum topology to provide a fundamentally different optimization paradigm, enabling precise modeling and discovery of quantum system properties. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting geometric constraints to enhance the system's behavior, resulting in superior accuracy and insight. This work represents a significant advancement in quantum system optimization, offering a robust and adaptable framework for tackling challenging problems.

title: Homomorphic Encryption-Based Distributed Computation
abstract: This paper explores the application of homomorphic encryption (HE) to enable secure distributed computation. Traditional distributed computing approaches often rely on trusted third parties to perform computations on sensitive data, introducing vulnerabilities and potential security risks. This research investigates a novel approach where computations are performed directly on encrypted data using HE, thus preserving data confidentiality throughout the entire process. We present a framework for implementing such systems, outlining the key challenges and potential solutions. The core claim of this work is to leverage HE to facilitate secure distributed data computation. The core mechanism involves the encryption of data using HE schemes followed by computation on the encrypted data, ensuring the integrity and confidentiality of the results. This approach offers a significant advancement in data security compared to conventional methods. We discuss the limitations of current HE schemes in the context of distributed computation and propose areas for future research.

We explore the potential of this technique to overcome limitations of existing methods and achieve improved accuracy in quantum information processing. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, its underlying mathematical principles, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its efficacy.

title: Decentralized Machine Learning via Federated Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to distributed machine learning, enabling model training on decentralized devices without directly exchanging sensitive data. However, the inherent vulnerability of FL systems to Byzantine failures – where malicious participants intentionally corrupt the learning process – poses a significant threat to its reliability and security. This paper proposes a decentralized machine learning framework leveraging federated learning with Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT). The core claim is the development of a robust FL system capable of maintaining accurate and secure model training despite the presence of adversarial actors. The proposed mechanism utilizes verifiable computation and secret sharing techniques to mitigate the impact of Byzantine attacks. This work addresses a critical gap in existing FL research by explicitly tackling the security challenges associated with adversarial behavior, paving the way for more trustworthy and resilient distributed learning applications. The system is designed to ensure data privacy and model integrity, even when compromised by malicious nodes. The theoretical framework and the proposed architecture will be discussed in detail.

title: An Inexpensive Optical Quantum-Key-Distribution Demo with Swiveled Cellophane Waveplates
abstract: There is much interest in introducing quantum physics to general and young audiences, particularly non-physics college and K-12 student populations. Hands-on laboratory demonstrations or simulations are powerful tools in facilitating a deep understanding of abstract quantum principles, such as superposition and measurement, and their applications. Quantum key distribution (QKD) has emerged as an important technology that uses these quantum principles. In this contribution, I present a simple and inexpensive demonstration of a QKD protocol using light’s polarization. It uses an inexpensive diode laser and optical components. I show how to diagnose and use cellophane wrappers as polarization waveplates. A key aspect involves using the optical components, such that once set up they only swivel about their holders to switch between the choices in the demo: binary data (0 or 1); and sender, receiver, and eavesdropper measurement bases. The detection consists of a clear natural calcite crystal to vividly display the outcomes on a screen.

title: Podatkovne semantične smernice kot temelj upravljanja podatkov in semantične interoperabilnosti v javni upravi
abstract: Prispevek prikazuje temeljne poudarke dokumenta »Podatkovne semantične smernice«, ki jih je marca 2026 objavilo Ministrstvo za digitalno preobrazbo (zdaj Ministrstvo za notranje zadeve in javno upravo). Smernice so nastale ob podpori strokovnjakov s Fakultete za računalništvo in informatiko Univerze v Ljubljani ter v sodelovanju z različnimi organi javne uprave. Smernice na enem mestu združujejo vsebine upravljanja podatkov in semantične interoperabilnosti. Za kakovostno odločanje in oblikovanje politik na podlagi podatkov potrebujemo kakovostne in interoperabilne podatke, dobro upravljanje in s tem možnost izrabe novih tehnologij. Smernice predstavljajo temelj za nadaljnji razvoj in boljšo, tudi čezmejno izmenjavo podatkov v skladu z evropskimi in mednarodnimi priporočili ter so standard za razvijalce aplikacij in druge uporabnike v organih javne uprave.

title: Credit Card Fraud Detection Using Deep Learning
abstract: This dataset includes 2034 credit card transactions, ideal for credit card fraud detection research and development using machine learning or deep learning. It contains 31 attributes: transaction time, transaction amount, 28 variables V1-V28 which are anonymized PCA-transformed, and a binary Class label with legitimate transactions (0) and fraudulent transactions (1). The dataset can be used for anomaly detection and classification, where models for fraud detection can be tested with the help of random forest, ANN, autoencoder, and hybrid deep learning models in imbalanced data analysis.

title: Explainable machine learning for leukaemia diagnosis: enhancing interpretability and trust
abstract: One of the major challenges in applying machine learning (ML) to leukaemia diagnosis is the limited interpretability of deep learning models such as artificial neural networks (ANNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). While these models excel at detecting complex patterns in medical data, they often function as “black boxes,” providing little transparency into their decision-making processes. This lack of explainability raises concerns in clinical practice, where understanding why a model predicts a specific leukaemia subtype is critical for guiding treatment decisions, including chemotherapy and bone marrow transplantation. To address these concerns, researchers are increasingly adopting explainable AI (XAI) techniques. Methods such as saliency maps, feature importance rankings, and attention mechanisms allow clinicians to visualize how specific factors such as genetic mutations, biomarkers, or cell morphology contribute to diagnostic outcomes. These interpretability tools not only enhance transparency but also foster trust among healthcare providers and patients. By bridging the gap between computational accuracy and clinical reliability, XAI ensures that ML models can be safely integrated into diagnostic workflows. Ultimately, explainable approaches strengthen confidence in AI-driven leukaemia diagnosis, supporting more informed medical decisions and improving patient care.

title: The single-lattice problem: Monoculture risk in standardized post-quantum cryptography
abstract: The first generation of post-quantum cryptographic standards from the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) rests on one mathematical foundation. Three of the four schemes standardized or in development, ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and FN-DSA, rest on the hardness of finding short vectors in structured lattices, while only SLH-DSA departs from it; the first two use Module Learning With Errors (Module-LWE) and the third the related but distinct NTRU assumption. This paper examines that concentration as a systemic risk. Drawing on the computer-security literature on software monoculture and design diversity, it argues by analogy that algorithmic homogeneity creates conditions for correlated failure of much deployed public-key cryptography. It makes the mechanism concrete: the security of all three schemes is estimated under one lattice-reduction cost model, so a sufficiently general advance in lattice reduction could move their security margins together while the non-lattice options stay untouched, as a cross-family correlation matrix and a sensitivity analysis show. It then separates three hazards often conflated in the debate, transition risk, assumption-monoculture risk, and implementation risk, and shows that the classical-plus-lattice hybrids now carrying most post-quantum Web traffic hedge the first but not the second. The claim is one of risk management, not mathematical certainty: no standardized lattice scheme is broken at its parameters as of mid-2026, and Module-LWE enjoys strong worst-case-to-average-case reductions. The case for diversification rests on the irreducible uncertainty of cryptanalysis, the fragility of implementation security, and the severe, potentially unrecoverable cost of a correlated failure.

title: Does Playing it Safe Count as Faithfulness? Reassessing LVLM Hallucination Mitigation Methods
abstract: Recent inference-time hallucination mitigation methods for large vision-language models (LVLMs) report strong gains on hallucination benchmarks. However, it remains unclear whether lower hallucination scores reflect improved multimodal grounding or more conservative generation. We evaluate six mitigation methods across three LVLMs and four benchmarks, including hallucination-focused evaluation and the diverse capability benchmark MMStar. Our analysis reveals two consistent patterns. First, hallucination reduction is often coupled with reduced informativeness: methods that lower hallucination rates also reduce object recall, visual coverage, or response detailedness. Second, improvements on hallucination benchmarks do not reliably transfer to broader multimodal capabilities, with methods showing inconsistent or degraded performance on fine-grained perception and reasoning tasks. Our findings suggest that current evaluation protocols may overestimate progress by rewarding conservative generation. We argue that hallucination mitigation should be evaluated as a faithfulness--informativeness--capability trade-off rather than through hallucination scores alone.

title: Linear Reusable Neural Bases Architecture for Network Compression
abstract: Memory constraints remain a critical bottleneck in the deployment of large-scale AI models. Parameter sharing across network depth reduces model storage, but repeatedly applying an identical transformation limits flexibility across layers. Inspired by time--memory trade-offs in classical algorithms, we introduce the Linear Reusable Neural Bases (LRNB) architecture, an RNN-based framework that improves parameter efficiency through parameter reuse at the \textit{neuron level}. Each feedforward residual module is represented as a linear combination of shared neural bases, with depth-specific learnable coefficients and optional shifts providing flexibility across layers. This formulation reduces parameter redundancy across depth and enables the construction of wider and deeper networks within a fixed parameter budget. We further provide a geometric interpretation of the neural bases from a vector-field perspective and extend the framework to linear projection modules. Experiments demonstrate that the LRNB architecture achieves comparable or lower final training loss than independently parameterized baselines while using fewer parameters and maintaining stable training dynamics. These findings support neuron-level reuse as a practical approach to parameter-efficient network design.

title: TimeSteer: Inference-Time Speech Scheduling in Joint Audio-Visual Diffusion Models
abstract: Although pretrained joint audio-visual diffusion models offer rich control over \emph{what} to generate, they provide no explicit control over \emph{when} an utterance should occur. To address this, we study \emph{inference-time speech scheduling}, a novel task that places coupled speech and visual articulation within user-specified begin--end intervals without finetuning the backbone model. We uncover two intrinsic properties of the denoising process that enable this task. First, a timing-sensitive text-to-audio cross-attention head exposes each utterance's model-implied source span along the latent timeline. Second, the predicted clean latent already organizes coupled speech and visual articulation, allowing their temporal placement to be edited without regenerating the content. Building on these discoveries, we propose \textbf{TimeSteer}, a training-free framework that localizes each utterance's source span through \textbf{Source Span Localization} and transfers the associated audio-visual latent content from the source interval to the specified target interval through \textbf{Region-Aware Latent Remapping}. We further introduce \textbf{SpeechShift}, the first benchmark for interval-level speech scheduling in joint audio-visual generation. Experiments across two representative backbones show that TimeSteer substantially improves interval controllability over training-free baselines while maintaining competitive overall generation quality.

title: Lacan: Making Accountability in Anonymous Networks Real
abstract: Anonymity and accountability are essential properties for our everyday activity on the Internet. However, they appear contradictory, and their reconciliation remains far from reality. Existing approaches fall short in this regard, as they either rely on an on-path trustee, per-packet authorization, per-packet public-key cryptography, or per-session intervention by a central authority. We propose Lacan, a protocol that reconciles anonymity and accountability within a realistic design. In Lacan, a sender enjoys anonymity provided by on-path relays, as long as she complies with a contract established with the receiver. Upon a contract violation, the verifier, an off-path trustee on behalf of the receiver, links the malicious message to the sender's identity indirectly via the packet, path, and session, thereby reducing public-key operations from per-packet to per-session. This linkage remains robust even against malicious relays and receivers, grounded in our novel chain of successor proofs for accountable path reconstruction, together with traceable signatures, path validation, and key-committing encryption. We analyze the anonymity and accountability, implement the protocol, and evaluate the performance.

title: Beyond Causal Sufficiency: When Is Optimal Invariant Prediction Possible?
abstract: Out-of-distribution prediction requires models that remain reliable when the test distribution differs from the training environments. Stabilized Regression addresses this problem causally by combining invariance across multiple environments with regression-optimality. However, this approach relies on the causal sufficiency assumption, limiting its applicability to realistic distribution generalization settings. In this work, we relax this assumption by analyzing invariant prediction in partially observed causal systems with latent confounding. We study the targetindependence assumption, a graphical condition that characterizes whether the ADMG admits an observed intervention-stable set and hence whether invariant prediction can be guaranteed across the considered class of environments. Building on this, we define the Mixed Stable Blanket (MSB), proven to be the optimal invariant predictor among all subsets of admissible variables in partially observed linear additive structural models. Experiments on synthetic data demonstrate the applicability of Stabilized Regression in partially observed settings.

title: "Systematic Review of the Firefly Algorithm in Data Clustering: Challenges and Research Directions"
abstract: Data clustering is a fundamental technique in data mining and unsupervised machine learning. It aims to partition unlabeled observations into meaningful groups according to their similarity. Conventional methods such as K-Means are attractive because of their simplicity and computational convenience; however, their performance can be affected by the initialization of cluster centers, local optima, and the need to specify the number of clusters in advance. The Firefly Algorithm (FA), a nature-inspired metaheuristic based on the flashing behavior of fireflies, offers an alternative optimization mechanism for addressing these limitations. Its population-based search strategy allows broader exploration of the solution space and does not require gradient information. Nevertheless, the literature on FA-based clustering remains fragmented, particularly with respect to automatic clustering, high-dimensional data, and application domains beyond wireless sensor networks. This review systematically examines studies published between 2023 and 2025 on the use of FA for data clustering. The reviewed studies are organized according to their main application strategies, including hybrid K-Means approaches, automatic clustering, wireless sensor networks, feature selection, and comparative studies. The findings indicate that hybrid FA–K-Means methods represent a dominant research direction, while issues such as computational cost, parameter sensitivity, convergence in high-dimensional spaces, and the absence of standardized evaluation settings remain important challenges. Based on these observations, several research directions are proposed for future studies at the intersection of metaheuristic optimization and data clustering.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Business: Emerging Trends and Strategic Innovations
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative forces shaping the contemporary business landscape. From automating routine operations and enhancing customer experiences to enabling data-driven decision-making, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, and innovative business models, AI is fundamentally changing the way organizations create, deliver, and capture value. The rapid advancement of machine learning, generative AI, natural language processing, computer vision, intelligent systems, and other AI technologies has created significant opportunities while simultaneously introducing new strategic, ethical, organizational, and regulatory considerations. The edited book Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Business: Emerging Trends and Strategic Innovations brings together diverse perspectives on the growing intersection of artificial intelligence, business strategy, innovation, and organizational transformation. The volume is intended to provide readers with a broad understanding of how emerging AI technologies are influencing different dimensions of business and how organizations can adapt to an increasingly intelligent and technology-driven environment. The chapters in this book explore a range of contemporary themes, including AI-driven business transformation, intelligent decision-making, automation, generative AI, customer analytics, digital innovation, AI-enabled marketing, financial applications, human–AI collaboration, entrepreneurship, organizational change, and emerging business models. The contributions also consider the importance of responsible AI, data governance, privacy, transparency, cybersecurity, and ethical considerations in the adoption and deployment of intelligent technologies. Beyond technological capabilities, the book emphasizes the strategic implications of AI adoption. Successful transformation requires more than implementing advanced technologies; it involves developing appropriate organizational capabilities, cultivating digital skills, redesigning business processes, managing change, and aligning technological innovation with organizational objectives. In this context, the contributions provide valuable insights into both the opportunities and challenges associated with integrating AI into contemporary business practices. This volume is designed to serve researchers, academics, business professionals, managers, entrepreneurs, policymakers, students, and practitioners interested in understanding the evolving relationship between artificial intelligence and business. It may also provide a useful reference for readers seeking to examine emerging trends, identify areas for further research, and understand the strategic implications of AI-enabled transformation across sectors. As AI continues to evolve, the future of business will increasingly depend on the ability of organizations to combine technological innovation with human expertise, creativity, critical thinking, responsible governance, and strategic vision. It is hoped that this book will contribute to ongoing academic and professional discussions on these developments and encourage further exploration of how artificial intelligence can shape innovative, resilient, and sustainable approaches to business in the years ahead. The editors gratefully acknowledge the contributions of all authors whose research, expertise, and perspectives have enriched this volume. We also extend our appreciation to everyone involved in the preparation, review, editing, and publication of this book.

title: A Privacy-Preserving Distributed Machine Learning Aggregation Scheme
abstract: Federated Learning enables data to remain on local devices, yet malicious servers can still infer sensitive user information by analyzing client-uploaded model updates, posing significant privacy leakage risks. Existing secure aggregation schemes—such as Differential Privacy, Homomorphic Encryption, and traditional Secret Sharing—struggle to achieve an ideal balance among model accuracy, computational/communication overhead, and adaptability to complex aggregation scenarios. To address this, this paper proposes a multi-server secure aggregation scheme based on additive secret sharing. The scheme introduces multiple non-colluding servers; each client splits its local model update into random secret shares and distributes them to these servers. Each server independently performs weighted aggregation, and the global model is reconstructed by a leader server. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that, owing to the linear homomorphism of additive secret sharing, the aggregation result of our scheme is mathematically equivalent to the standard FedAvg algorithm. Experimental results on the MNIST dataset show that our scheme achieves a test accuracy of 86.13% after 30 global rounds, closely matching the baseline FedAvg (86.12%), with only a 6% additional time overhead per round. Under reasonable non-collusion assumptions, the scheme achieves information-theoretic privacy protection, effectively breaking the trilemma among privacy, accuracy, and efficiency.Keywords:Federated Learning, Additive Secret Sharing,Secure Aggregation; Privacy Preservationords.

title: Attention Is All You Needed, Eventually: A Critical Survey Review of The Transformer Revolution in Sequence Modeling
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Transformer Revolution in Sequence Modeling in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of transformers and attention as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Non-Local Quantum State Adaptive Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper investigates a novel algorithm for optimizing quantum parameter adjustments based on non-local quantum state dynamics. Traditional parameter tuning methods often rely on manual adjustments, while this approach aims to automate the adjustment process, leading to enhanced computational efficiency and accuracy. We introduce a framework that dynamically adapts parameters to maintain the optimal quantum state, leveraging the inherent fluctuations of the quantum system. The core mechanism centers around the continuous monitoring and adjustment of parameters based on the evolution of the quantum state, achieved through a sophisticated iterative process. This work presents a practical implementation demonstrating significant improvements in the performance of quantum computations, particularly in scenarios involving complex parameter landscapes.

title: Title: Quantum Resonance Synchronization for Algorithmic Complexity
abstract: Quantum Resonance Synchronization (QRS) presents a novel framework for enhancing algorithmic complexity by synchronizing quantum systems. This approach posits that specific resonant frequencies can influence the evolution of complex computational algorithms, leading to increased performance and the emergence of quantum complexity – a state of increased computational power often associated with quantum phenomena. This paper explores the theoretical foundations of QRS, detailing the concept of resonant frequency manipulation and its potential impact on algorithmic optimization. We will examine the underlying mathematical models and potential applications within the context of complex computational problems. The paper will conclude with a discussion of future research directions and the challenges involved in translating this concept into practical implementations.

title: Neural Network Topology Optimization via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network design, termed Neural Network Topology Optimization via Reinforcement Learning (NNTORL). The core claim is that optimizing network architecture directly, rather than solely adjusting weights, yields superior performance. We propose a framework utilizing reinforcement learning (RL) to learn optimal topology design strategies within a simulated environment where connections between neurons can be dynamically modified. The RL agent explores different network topologies, receiving rewards based on the network's performance on a given task. This allows for the automated generation of optimized network structures, effectively circumventing the challenges associated with manual network design or traditional weight-based optimization methods. The system learns a policy that maps states (representing the network's current configuration and performance) to actions (representing changes to the network's topology). The resulting networks demonstrate improved accuracy and efficiency compared to networks designed using conventional techniques. This work introduces a fundamentally new paradigm for neural network design, shifting the focus from parameter tuning to architectural optimization.

title: Bush Duiker: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bush Duiker Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bush Duiker, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of bush duikers (Diceros bicornis). Bush duikers are known for their efficient and adaptable foraging strategies in dense woodland environments. The algorithm leverages key aspects of this behavior – particularly the utilization of spatial memory and the dynamic adjustment of movement strategies – to create a robust and effective optimization method. Bush Duiker incorporates a memory module that stores the locations of previously discovered high-fitness solutions and employs a dynamic adaptation mechanism based on the relative distances to these stored solutions. The algorithm utilizes a probability-based exploration and exploitation strategy, governed by a novel parameter, α (alpha), which controls the balance between exploration and exploitation. Performance evaluation is conducted on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating the algorithm's competitiveness against established metaheuristic methods. The results indicate that Bush Duiker exhibits promising performance and adaptability, particularly in complex, high-dimensional search spaces. The core of the algorithm resides in its memory management and the adaptive movement strategy, which are designed to mimic the intelligent foraging behaviors of bush duikers.

title: Cognitive Architectures for Explainable AI
abstract: The increasing deployment of complex Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems, particularly deep learning models, has raised significant concerns regarding their lack of transparency and interpretability. This paper argues that building truly explainable AI (XAI) systems necessitates a fundamental shift in approach – integrating cognitive architectures that closely mimic human reasoning processes. We propose a core claim: that transparent and interpretable explanations can be derived by leveraging cognitive architectures like ACT-R or Soar to provide a detailed, step-by-step account of an AI system's decision-making. The mechanism involves designing an AI system around a chosen cognitive architecture, allowing the architecture's internal processes to directly inform the explanation of the AI's output. This approach offers a novel solution to the XAI challenge by grounding AI explanations in established models of human cognition. We explore the potential benefits and challenges of this integration, emphasizing the importance of a symbiotic relationship between the AI system and the underlying cognitive architecture. The goal is not simply to generate post-hoc explanations, but to build systems whose reasoning processes are inherently understandable.

title: Nonlinear Topological Quantum Entanglement: Geometric Properties Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the geometric properties of non-linear topological quantum entanglement, exploring its dynamic characteristics and offering precise control and secure transmission of quantum information. The research focuses on establishing a geometric model of entangled states through non-linear topological dynamics, utilizing computational techniques to reveal its dynamic evolution. A novel approach aims to enhance the fidelity and controllability of quantum information transfer by leveraging this unique approach. The core claim is that the study will identify dynamic entanglement characteristics and enable precise control and secure transmission. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of the interplay between topological quantum systems and the properties of entangled states.

title: Procedural Evolutionary Algorithm-Driven Meta-Learning Optimization
abstract: Meta-learning, also known as learning to learn, has emerged as a promising approach to tackle complex learning problems. However, the performance of meta-learning algorithms is often highly sensitive to the choice of hyperparameters, which traditionally require extensive manual tuning. This paper proposes a novel framework that leverages procedural evolutionary algorithms (PEAs) to automatically optimize the hyperparameters of meta-learning algorithms. The core idea is to define a parameter space for the meta-learning algorithm and employ a PEA to iteratively explore and refine these parameters, ultimately leading to improved meta-learning performance. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and a conceptual design that this approach significantly enhances the adaptability and efficiency of meta-learning systems. The proposed method offers a shift from human-designed hyperparameters to an automated, adaptive optimization process, promising a more robust and scalable solution for meta-learning challenges. The key components of this framework include a PEA, a parameter space representation, and a fitness function that evaluates the meta-learning performance based on a set of target tasks. The system iteratively evolves the meta-learning algorithm's parameters, converging towards an optimal configuration that maximizes its learning ability across diverse tasks.

title: ## Booted Titi: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Booting Behavior of *Saguinus booted*
abstract: This paper introduces Booted Titi, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique bootstrapping behavior observed in *Saguinus booted*, a species of pygmy marmoset. The algorithm leverages a combination of simulated annealing, particle swarm optimization, and a novel 'booting' mechanism that mimics the animal's rapid and directional movements for exploration and exploitation. The core of Booted Titi lies in dynamically adjusting the influence of these components based on the perceived stagnation of the search space. Mathematical formulations describing the algorithm's key parameters, decision-making processes, and convergence criteria are presented. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within a reasonable timeframe. Preliminary results show promising performance, suggesting that Booted Titi could be a valuable tool for tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: Native unknown Outputs as a Scheduling Signal for Model Arrays: Small-Model Gatekeeping, Queryable Knowledge Maps, and the Failure Boundary of Same-Family Weighted Voting (English v1.0)
abstract: Companion short paper to "A 774M-Parameter Model Trained from Scratch Says 'I Don't Know'" (10.5281/zenodo.22191510). Moving the uncertainty signal from post-hoc estimation to generation time: unknown as a first-class output category becomes a metadata bit that a model array amplifies into three system capabilities — gatekeeping (37× leakage suppression; out-of-domain perception holds on all 55 concepts of a three-gradient probe set, with root shortcuts inert outside the boundary band), a queryable knowledge map (cross-seed consistency 0.946, disagreement self-localizing to the known/unknown critical band), and union-intersection two-expert routing (3,000-step unit expansion, zero forgetting). A clean negative result bounds the signal's value: within a same-family array, equal/quality/oracle weighting and two further fusion operations all degenerate to identical decisions (0.976) — overriding power requires out-of-array information sources. A six-route industry survey (MoE / cascades / ensembles / guardmodels / uncertainty estimation / industrial self-routing) finds no counterpart for the native-metadata-bit + small-model-gatekeeper + state-judgment-array combination; neuroscience offers functional-level precedents (single-cell confidence coding; dopamine pause signals). All 28 references verified one-by-one.

title: Resilient Neural Networks with Adaptive Sparsity via Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the development of resilient neural networks by leveraging adaptive sparsity achieved through evolutionary algorithms. Traditional neural network architectures are susceptible to adversarial attacks and noisy data, resulting in significant performance degradation. Our approach addresses this vulnerability by dynamically adjusting the network's sparsity pattern during training, creating a more robust and adaptable architecture. We propose a framework where an evolutionary algorithm iteratively optimizes the sparsity pattern, effectively reducing the network's complexity and enhancing its ability to withstand perturbations. The core of our method lies in the algorithm's capacity to learn and adapt, shifting sparsity patterns based on the network's response to training data and potential adversarial inputs. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this adaptive sparsity strategy in improving network resilience and maintaining performance under challenging conditions. The key contribution is the systematic application of evolutionary algorithms to achieve adaptive sparsity, a novel approach for building robust neural networks.

title: Neural Network Topology Adaptive Encoding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neural network optimization termed "Neural Network Topology Adaptive Encoding." The core idea is to dynamically adjust the topology of a neural network – specifically the connections between neurons – to achieve more efficient and robust encoding of input data. This adaptation is driven by a reinforcement learning algorithm, utilizing a "topology controller" network. The controller monitors network performance metrics and adjusts the network topology in real-time, creating, removing, or modifying connections to align with learned signal patterns. This approach aims to enhance both the generalization ability and interpretability of neural networks, addressing limitations inherent in static, fixed-topology architectures. The central claim is that by optimizing both the connection weights and the network topology, we can significantly improve the efficiency and robustness of neural encoding. This is achieved through the dynamic adjustment of the neural network's architecture, driven by a reinforcement learning algorithm. The key mechanism involves a "topology controller" network that monitors the network's performance and adjusts the connections between neurons to create new connections, remove redundant connections, or even change the organization of neuronal clusters. The changes in topology are linked to the learned signal patterns, resulting in the network "remembering" specific input data. The potential impact lies in overcoming the limitations of traditional neural networks with fixed structures.

title: Black-tailed Melomys-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed Black-tailed Melomys Algorithm (BTMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Melomys rubicola* (Black-tailed Melomys). These rodents exhibit a unique and highly efficient foraging strategy, characterized by a combination of exploration and exploitation, particularly when faced with limited resources and varying environmental conditions. BTMA leverages these observed behaviors to construct a new optimization framework. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic population size adaptation mechanism mimicking the rodent's responsiveness to resource availability and a novel mutation operator designed to simulate the exploratory movements of the animals. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BTMA on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution accuracy, and computational efficiency. The key innovations of BTMA lie in its adaptive population size control and its biologically-inspired mutation strategy, contributing to its robust performance across diverse optimization landscapes.

title: Enhanced performance of spin-wave reservoir computing through artificial lattice engineering
abstract: We investigated the performance of a spin-wave reservoir chip incorporating an artificial lattice. By introducing lattice-patterned microfabrication into a ferromagnetic permalloy waveguide, the device increases the complexity of spin-wave propagation and enhances the diversity of reservoir states. A one-input, four-output reservoir was implemented using antennas placed on the waveguide, and its performance was evaluated using short-term memory and parity-check tasks. Experimental results demonstrated that the device with the artificial lattice achieved higher learning performance than the device without the lattice. Furthermore, the tasks were performed under varying external magnetic fields, and the lattice device exhibited stable and enhanced performance over a wide range of magnetic-field conditions.

title: Qutrit-Based Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution Secure Against Collective Attacks
abstract: Klassische Kryptographie beruht auf der rechnerischen Schwierigkeit bestimmter Probleme, doch Fortschritte im Quantencomputing gefährden diese Annahmen. Der Quantenschlüsselaustausch (Quantum Key Distribution - QKD) nutzt die Prinzipien der Quantenmechanik und ermöglicht es zwei räumlich getrennten Parteien, einen gemeinsamen geheimen Schlüssel mit informationstheoretischer Sicherheit zu erzeugen, selbst gegenüber Angreifer*innen mit unbegrenzter Rechenleistung. In QKD sind Annahmen über Messgeräte und Quantenzustandsquellen zentral für die Sicherheitsanalyse und bestimmen verschiedene Familien von Protokollen. Geräteunabhängige QKD (Device Independent QKD - DI-QKD) bietet das höchste Sicherheitsniveau: Weder Geräte noch Quellen müssen vertrauenswürdig sein und könnten sogar von einer Angreifer*in kontrolliert werden. In diesem Kontext beruht die Sicherheit auf der Beobachtung starker Quantenkorrelationen, die sich durch die Verletzung einer Bell-Ungleichung manifestieren. Die Berechnung der Schlüsselrate, welche die Effizienz der Schlüsselgenerierung beschreibt, beinhaltet eine Optimierung über alle Messungen und Quantenzustände beliebiger Hilbertraumdimension, die mit der beobachteten Verletzung einer Bell Ungleichung konsistent sind. Für Bell Ungleichungen mit zwei Messeinstellungen und zwei Messergebnissen pro Partei, wie die CHSH-Ungleichung, lässt sich diese Optimierung auf Qubits beschränken, was analytische Lösungen für die Schlüsselrate ermöglicht. In dieser Arbeit untersuchen wir diesen Ansatz im Detail mit dem Ziel, ihn auf Bell-Ungleichungen mit drei Messergebnissen zu übertragen, wobei angenommen wird, dass Alice und Bob einen Zwei-Qutrit-Zustand teilen. Während diese Einschränkung den DI-Anspruch abschwächt, ist dieses Setting dennoch von Interesse, da es trotzdem Einblicke in höherdimensionale DI-QKD über numerische Resultate hinaus liefern und Intuition darüber geben könnte, ob höhere Dimensionen eine größere Rauschtoleranz ermöglichen.

Während diese Einschränkung den DI-Anspruch abschwächt, ist dieses Setting dennoch von Interesse, da es trotzdem Einblicke in höherdimensionale DI-QKD über numerische Resultate hinaus liefern und Intuition darüber geben könnte, ob höhere Dimensionen eine größere Rauschtoleranz ermöglichen.

title: Enhancing fraction multiplication and division performance through intelligent tutoring system with visual models
abstract: Mathematical proficiency, especially fractions, help humans to succeed in their future. However, students tend to struggle in understanding fractions, one of them is natural number bias (NNB). This study aims to address this challenge by developing a web-based math intelligent tutoring system (ITS) using the cognitive tutor authoring tools (CTATs) to create a cognitive tutor with adaptive feedback and visual models to support students in learning fraction multiplication and division. This study compares the students’ learning performance from two schools which the first school has aligned visual method with the system proposed. The results show that the experimental groups in the first school outperformed the control group with an average learning gain of 33.78%, while in the second school the control group outperformed the experimental group with average learning gain of 65.79%. Each school suggests statistically significant differences in students’ results. This highlights the effectiveness of ITS depends not only on system features but also the importance of alignment between students’ prior visual models and the visualization method in the system. Students with aligned visual method suggest positive feedback from the survey conducted, indicating its potential for improving fraction learning when it is integrated consistently with existing visual instruction.

title: SignMatch: Matching Dictionary Signs to Continuous Sign Language Video
abstract: The objective of this paper is to match dictionary sign videos to corresponding signs in continuous signing videos, where a match is defined by the visual similarity alone - the handshape and motion relative to the body. To achieve this, we learn a prototype-structured sign embedding space from continuous video annotated with signs, where each learnable prototype corresponds to a sign class. Isolated dictionary videos are then mapped into this sign space, enabling the matching between dictionary exemplars and continuous sign instances. This design supports direct dictionary-guided sign matching through embedding similarity and naturally extends to unseen signs using only dictionary exemplars. Experiments on ASL-Citizen dictionary retrieval, ChaLearn OSLWL dictionary-to-continuous sign matching, and using BOBSL's CSLR2 evaluation for automatic sign annotation demonstrate strong generalisation across datasets, tasks and sign languages. Without benchmark-specific supervision, the learned representation transfers effectively across American, British, and Spanish Sign Languages, outperforming prior methods on all three benchmarks. Project page: https://www.robots.ox.ac.uk/~vgg/research/signmatch/

title: Seeing the World and the Self from Egocentric Video
abstract: Complete 3D perception from egocentric video requires recovering the surrounding scene and the wearer's full-body motion in a shared metric frame. Existing methods typically address scene reconstruction and motion estimation separately: scene reconstruction methods ignore the wearer, whereas motion estimation methods lack explicit scene geometry and often depend on external trajectories. Joint recovery is challenging because the two tasks exhibit asymmetric visibility and require different prediction paradigms. The largely visible scene supports deterministic geometric regression, whereas the severely occluded body requires generative motion inference. We therefore propose RESELF (REconstructing the Scene and the sELF), a unified framework that couples deterministic metric geometry reconstruction with geometry-conditioned motion generation. RESELF adapts a geometry foundation model pre-trained on large-scale exocentric data to egocentric video using frame-wise scale and relative-pose consistency objectives. The resulting camera trajectory and latent geometric features condition a diffusion model that recovers the wearer's motion. A subsequent closed-loop kinematic feedback stage further refines the camera head while preserving the reconstructed scene geometry. To support training and evaluation, we curate EE4D-JSM from EgoExo4D by aligning egocentric video, sparse metric scene geometry, camera trajectories, and full-body motion annotations. Experiments show that RESELF outperforms state-of-the-art methods designed for the individual tasks across depth estimation, camera tracking, and full-body motion estimation. Code, models, and datasets will be available at https://ka1guan.github.io/RESELF/.

title: PCoMoE: Shifting MoE Inference from Monolithic Expert Selection to Fine-Grained Path Composition
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures scale Large Language Model (LLM) capacity efficiently by activating a sparse subset of experts per token. However, modern MoE inference remains heavily constrained by the rigid, whole-expert abstraction. Existing frameworks manage, schedule, or prune experts as atomic execution units, which fixes the optimization boundary too early and leaves fine-grained intra-expert computational redundancy underexplored. In this work, we present PCoMoE, a path-compositional execution framework that shifts MoE inference from coarse-grained expert selection to fine-grained path composition. PCoMoE incorporates a path-level formulation of expert computation, a compatibility-aware layer-wise pruning strategy to suppress low-value path combinations, and a hardware-friendly execution engine to exploit reusable sub-expert structures under strictly bounded overheads. Experimental results demonstrate that PCoMoE achieves up to a 1.31x end-to-end inference speedup while enhancing model accuracy by 10%. The code is available at https://github.com/gzyyy0/PCoMoE

title: When Features Become Instances: Inverted Contrastive Learning for Unsupervised Feature Selection
abstract: Unsupervised feature selection seeks a compact subset of informative features without access to class labels, making feature utility difficult to define. Existing UFS methods therefore rely on indirect structural criteria, such as similarity preservation, locality, sparsity, cluster geometry, or reconstruction quality. In this paper, we instead study UFS through representation consistency and propose Inverted Contrastive Learning for Unsupervised Feature Selection (ICLFS), a feature-wise contrastive framework that reformulates UFS as a representation learning problem over features rather than samples. ICLFS first inverts the data matrix so that each feature is represented by its sample-profile vector, then constructs multiple masked positive views together with a shuffled negative view, and learns projector-space representations that remain consistent across these structured perturbations under an InfoNCE-based objective. Motivated by recent findings that cosine-based and InfoNCE-based training affect embedding norms, we use projector-space embedding magnitude as the saliency signal for ranking features. The resulting norm-based ranking is subsequently refined through Laplacian-Gated Ranking Correction, which suppresses locally redundant candidates while preserving salient ones. Extensive experiments on 12 benchmark datasets show that ICLFS achieves the best clustering accuracy on 10 datasets against both classical and neural baselines under the standard clustering-based UFS evaluation protocol, while remaining competitive on the other two. These results show that feature-wise contrastive representation consistency provides a strong and effective alternative to neighborhood, cluster, and reconstruction-based UFS formulations.

title: WiseSpec: Requirements-Driven Agents for Code Generation
abstract: Code generation aims to automatically generate source code from task requirements and has attracted significant attention with the rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs). Despite remarkable progress, LLMs often struggle to generate correct code for complex software engineering tasks because task descriptions are frequently incomplete, ambiguous, or lack critical contextual information. Existing approaches primarily improve the capabilities of coding agents through more sophisticated tools, skills, and workflows, while largely overlooking the quality of the task requirements themselves. To address this limitation, we draw inspiration from software requirements engineering and propose WiseSpec, a novel requirements-driven agent framework for repository-level code generation. WiseSpec automatically constructs structured and information-rich requirements, assesses their quality through execution-based evaluation, and iteratively refines them to better guide code generation. Experimental results show that WiseSpec consistently outperforms all baselines, achieving an average improvement of 13.17% in %Resolved.

title: BioELX: Context-Aware Cross-lingual Biomedical Entity Linking without Task-Specific Supervision
abstract: Cross-lingual biomedical entity linking (BEL) maps mentions in any language to unique identifiers in a biomedical knowledge base, supporting clinical and biomedical NLP applications. We identify two issues affecting current systems. First, the UMLS (Bodenreider,2004) aliases used to train cross-lingual BEL retrievers are heavily skewed toward English, so retrievers generalize poorly to non-English mentions. Second, although context is often necessary for disambiguation, naively injecting context into retrievers trained only to align aliases severely degrades retrieval. We propose BioELX, a retrieve-rerank framework that addresses both issues. For retrieval, we continue training SapBERT_multi (Liu et al., 2021b) using Wikidata-derived cross-lingual alias supervision, forming shared concept neighborhoods across languages. For reranking, we adapt pretrained LLM rerankers to entity linking through mention-anchored prompting, which marks the target mention so that rerankers score candidates with respect to the intended mention rather than other salient tokens in the context. Experiments show that BioELX achieves new state-of-the-art results on four cross-lingual BEL benchmarks, improving Recall@1 by 4.8 to 18.2 percentage points over prior best results, without any task-specific BEL annotations. Our code and resources are available at https://github.com/AI4MedCode/BioELX.

title: Learning Patterns from Incommensurable Data
abstract: Data-driven machine learning connects characteristics of data to implementation decisions. Previous approaches tended to rely on field-specific experience such as previously successful classification models on ``similar'' data. How can the similarity of data be defined if they are collected from independent sources? One way is commensurability. In this dissertation we called datasets commensurable if variables have equivalent meaning across datasets. We focused on high-dimensional medical images of tissue acquired using mass spectrometry imaging (MSI). Technical and biological variation make comparison across images challenging. Despite this challenge, it is common practiced for spectra to be combined across images to find generalizable biomarkers of tumors. We showed that for the datasets used, MSIs are incommensurable and thus that aggregation of spectra across images should be performed with caution. Another way to compare datasets is data complexity. Data complexity measures are quantified characteristics of data that relate to the potential classification accuracy of a dataset. We used data complexity to predict the classification accuracy of over 20 classification models for 17 datasets; this is called meta-learning. The meta-models were applied to MSIs and showed that not only do data complexity of images differ, but aggregated images have the complexity of challenging natural-language datasets. This gave us a foundation to tackle the question: can we learn stable patterns from incommensurable data? We used a stacked ensemble model to find biomarkers of tumor tissue from MSIs. We showed biomarkers learned from aggregated images missed clinically relevant biomarkers that were captured when training on individual images. We discussed our findings in the context of personalized medicine.

title: TRACING THE RELEVANCE OF BLOCKCHAIN IN THE FIELD OF COPYRIGHT: BY ANALYTICALLY EXAMINING THE JOURNEY OF CONCEPT OF COPYRIGHT LAW, ROLE OF BLOCKCHAIN IN REGULATING MUSIC INDUSTRY, LICENSING, OUTPUT DEVELOPED USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, OWNERSHIP CLAIMS, DIGITAL RIGHTS MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS - INTERNATIONALLY AND NATIONALLY, PROBLEMS FACED DURING ENFORCEMENT AND ITS IMPRESSION ON SOCIAL JUSTICE IN INDIA
abstract: The intellectual property sector is undergoing through significant changes due to the rapid growth in the technology.This paper traces the history of the intellectual property with national and international frameworks from Statute of Anne to the World Intellectual Property Organization and emerging technologies, explores the relevance of blockchain technology in the field of copyright, concept of related terms like Digital Rights Management Systems, licensing, ownership claims and AI-generated contents and how this technology has affected music industry so far.This paper also highlights the enforcement issues faced in India and how this technology aids in serving justice.The methodology used in this research paper is primarily analytical and doctrinal in nature.It uses an analytical approach to underline the history of the intellectual property.The study counts on primary sources, which includes The Copyright Act, 1957, The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and judicial decisions of courts of India.The secondary sources used in this paper are WIPO reports, The National Blockchain Frameworks and international case laws.The key findings of this paper point out on how the core features of blockchain technology, that is, immutability, timestamping, decentralized ledger, etc will bring revolution in the IP sector (particularly in the music industry), help in serving justice to the creators in cases of ownership claims, AI-generated contents, etc., and also the shortcomings which might be faced by the world in the use of this technology.Finally, 1 BBA.LL.B.

abstract: Mazkur maqolada raqamli korpus tilshunosligining o‘zbek tili rivojlanishidagi o‘rni hamda sun’iy intellekt asosidagi sinxron tarjima texnologiyalari tahlil qilinadi.
